建設目的no一tsuniha、車体規格ga小saku編成長mo短ikotokara輸送力増強ni限界noaru丸no内線no混雑緩和gaata。Ikebukuro Stationno乗ri換ega便利deatatame、日比谷線ni対suru千代田線同様、混雑no緩和ni大kiku寄与shita。

mata、1974年（Showa49年）no銀座一丁目 - Ikebukuro Station間noopenedniatari、丸no内線中野坂上駅、日比谷線恵比寿駅ni次ide、Ikebukuro Stationni4基、銀座一丁目駅ni2基no自動改札機ga設置sareta。koreha、当該区間deha他線tono改札内連絡ganakatatame、集改札自動化no実証実験線区toshite好適deatatamedearu。両端駅dearuIkebukuro Station、銀座一丁目駅以外niha自動改札機ha設置sarenakataga、有楽町線no全駅de磁気化券ga発売sareteori、普通乗車券niyoru出場nimo対応shiteita。shikashi、当時ha他no路線deno乗車券no磁気化ga進ndeorazu、効率的na運用gadekinakatakotokara、営団成増（現, 地下鉄成増）延伸時ni一旦撤去sare、当時no試miha失敗ni終wateiru。sono他、大手町駅de採用sareta案内sainshisutemuwo全面的ni採用shita。

13号線nitsuiteha新線Ikebukuro Stationkara西早稲田、新宿三丁目wo経te渋谷駅ni至rurutoga2008年（Heisei20年）6月14日ni東京metoro副都心線toshiteopenedshita。sarani、副都心線ha2013年（Heisei25年）3月16日kara渋谷駅kara東急東横線経由deminatomirai線元町, 中華街駅made乗ri入rewo開始shita。mata、今後no整備計画toshite8号線nitsuitehaToyosu Stationkara分岐shite野田市駅madeno延伸計画gaaru（詳細ha"都市高速鉄道8号線延伸構想"no節wo参照）。kono区間hakatsute営団地下鉄ga1982年（Showa57年）1月29日niToyosu Station - 亀有間 (14.7 km) no地方鉄道事業免許wo申請shiteitaga。免許no交付hasareteinakata。営団地下鉄no計画deha、1985年度kara1992年度no工期de、建設費用ha2,720億円wo見込ndeita。sono後、2022年（Reiwa4年）ni東京metorohaToyosu Station - 住吉間no鉄道事業許可wo申請shi、同年国土交通大臣kara許可sareta。

有楽町線ha、東京地下鉄nioite最初ni埼玉県ni延伸sareta路線dearu。東京地下鉄de東京23区外ni延biteiru路線ha、当線tono重複区間gaaru副都心線wo除kuto当線to東西線nomideari、都営地下鉄mo含meta東京no地下鉄全路線demo他ni都営新宿線wo加eta3路線nomidearu。
章节.路線名:
"有楽町線"no名称ha、1973年（Showa48年）11月1日kara同年12月15日madeno期間de一般公募ga行ware、30,591通no応募gaari、2,519種類no路線名ga提案sareta。

sono時no得票数第1位ha"Kōjimachi Station線"deata。shikashi、"麹"no漢字ga当用漢字（当時）denaitame難shiku親shiminikuitoiukoto、2位"有楽町線", 5位"有楽線"nadono"有楽町"ni関suru名称gatsuita内容ga記載saretamonoga多katakoto、将来的ni湾岸eriani延伸suru予定deari（選定当時）、延伸開通後有楽町ga路線no中間点ni位置surukotokara、1974年（Showa49年）1月9日ni"有楽町線"to決定shita。

応募no中niha"kangaru線"（"有"楽町, 池"袋" → 有袋類no連想）toiumonomoatatoiu。
章节.建設費用: 当路線noWakōshi Station - 新木場間（有楽町線新線toshite建設sareta区間ha含manai）no建設費用ha総額4,920億円dearu。sono内訳ha土木関係費ga2,961億5,032万8,000円、電気関係費ga448億2,681万2,000円、車両関係費ga658億5,965万4,000円、sono他ga851億6,320万6,000円tonateiru。
章节.軌道構造: 当路線dehaJNR（当時, Japanese National Railways (JNR)）wo除ki、地下鉄, 私鉄de初mete60 kgreruwo採用shita（本線部）。60 kgreruwo採用surukotode、reruno強度ga1.5倍、耐用年数ha4 - 6年長kunaru。軌道構造ha地下区間deha従来kara直結軌道wo採用shitekitaga、振動, 騒音ga大kiikotokara、本路線deha新tani"防振makuragi構造"wo採用shita（民有地近辺）。初期hareruto枕木no間nigomupadowo、枕木ha防振gomude覆umonodeataga、新富町opened以降、枕木部hareru支持部下ni防振gomu、防振pado、防振kushonkara構成sareru防振装置wo敷ki、reru間下wo中空toshita新shii構造wo採用shita。barasuto軌道区間nioitemo、軌道下ni防振matomataha防振shitowo敷ki、izuremo振動, 騒音低減ni大kina効果wo発揮shita。

1962年（Showa37年）10月16日：第8号線、谷原町 - 江東橋間（中村橋 - 錦糸町間）no地方鉄道敷設免許wo申請。

 7月22日：第8号線、谷原町 - 江東橋間（中村橋 - 錦糸町間）no地方鉄道敷設免許申請wo取ri下ge、上鷺宮 - 音羽間（中村橋 - Gokokuji Station間）no地方鉄道敷設免許wo申請。

 3月1日：都市交通審議会答申第15号ga答申sare、新tani第13号線（志木 - Wakōshi Station - 成増 - 向原 - Ikebukuro Station方面）ga制定sareru。
 10月23日：上鷺宮 - 音羽間（中村橋 - Gokokuji Station間）no地方鉄道敷設免許no申請wo取ri下ge。
 1974年（Showa49年）
 1月9日：第8号線wo有楽町線to呼称決定。
 10月30日：Ikebukuro Station - 銀座一丁目間opened。opened当初no同区間no運賃ha80円。7000系5両編成de運行sareta。tadashi、Ikebukuro Station、銀座一丁目駅ha一部工事ga遅reteori、当初ha仮施設de営業shiteita。1976年（Showa51年）6月niIkebukuro Stationnokonkosu部to銀座一丁目駅ga完成、同年8月niIkebukuro Stationplatform部分ga完成shita。
 1975年（Showa50年）9月2日：第13号線Wakōshi Station - 成増間toIkebukuro Station - 渋谷間no地方鉄道敷設免許申請oyobi第8号線向原 - Ikebukuro Station間no工事方法no一部変更（向原 - Ikebukuro Station間wo複々線tosuru）認可wo申請。
 1976年（Showa51年）
 3月1日：銀座一丁目 - 新富町間no建設工事ni着手。
 8月11日：第13号線Wakōshi Station - 成増間no地方鉄道敷設免許取得oyobi第8号線向原 - Ikebukuro Station間no工事方法no一部変更（向原 - Ikebukuro Station間wo複々線tosuru）ga認可sareru。tadashi、Ikebukuro Station - 渋谷間no地方鉄道敷設免許no交付ha保留tonata。

 1979年（Showa54年）10月24日：新富町 - 湾岸（現, 新木場）間no地方鉄道敷設免許wo申請。
 1980年（Showa55年）
 3月27日：銀座一丁目 - 新富町間opened。
 9月26日：新富町 - 湾岸間no地方鉄道敷設免許wo取得。
 1982年（Showa57年）
 1月29日：Toyosu Station - 亀有間 (14.7 km) no地方鉄道敷設免許wo申請。tadashi、免許no交付hasareteinai。

 7月30日：第13号線区間tonaruWakōshi Station - Ikebukuro Station間nitsuite、"有楽町線"to呼称surukotowo正式決定。

 6月1日：車両冷房no運用wo開始。
 6月8日：新富町 - 新木場間opened、全線opened。

 1994年（Heisei6年）12月7日：有楽町線新線小竹向原 - 新線Ikebukuro Station（現, Ikebukuro Station）間opened。同時ni西武有楽町線新桜台 - 練馬間ga単線deopenedshitakotoniyori、練馬駅made乗ri入re開始。西武鉄道no車両no乗ri入rewo開始。
 1995年（Heisei7年）3月20日：地下鉄sarin事件ni関連shi午前no運転wo休止、午後kara再開。
 1998年（Heisei10年）3月26日：西武有楽町線ga全線複線化sare同線経由de西武Ikebukuro Station線tono相互乗ri入re開始（乗ri入re区間wo飯能駅made延長）。
 2002年（Heisei14年）10月12日：Ikebukuro Station - 新富町駅間de新CS-ATCwo使用開始。
 2004年（Heisei16年）4月1日：帝都高速度交通営団no民営化niyori東京地下鉄（東京metoro）ni承継。営団赤塚駅to営団成増駅wosorezore地下鉄赤塚駅to地下鉄成増駅ni改称。
 2005年（Heisei17年）10月31日：女性専用車両導入。
 2006年（Heisei18年）9月1日：10000系営業運転開始。
 2007年（Heisei19年）10月27日：Wakōshi Station - Ikebukuro Station, 小竹向原駅 - 新線Ikebukuro Station（当時）間de新CS-ATCwo使用開始。
 2008年（Heisei20年）
 5月3日：小田急特急romansuka（60000形"MSE"）乗ri入re開始。
 6月14日：副都心線openedni伴i、Wakōshi Station - 小竹向原駅間ga同線tono共用区間tonari、有楽町線新線小竹向原駅 - 新線Ikebukuro Station間ga副都心線ni編入sareru。準急列車運転開始。

 3月6日：準急列車ga廃止sareru。

 Heisei22年度事業計画nioite、sudeni設置済mino小竹向原駅wo除ku全駅ni順次platformdoawo設置surukotowo表明。mata、小竹向原駅 - 千川駅間ni連絡線wo設置surunado遅延対策ni乗ri出sukotomo発表shita。
 2011年（Heisei23年）
 2月23日：kono日kara地下鉄成増, 地下鉄赤塚両駅ni発車merodeiga導入sareta。以後、platformdoaga稼働shiteiru駅kara順次発車merodeino使用ga開始sareteiru。
 9月25日：小田急romansukano乗ri入rewo休止。
 10月4日：8時54分goro、小竹向原駅dekonkuritoga落下shi、信号keburuwo切断suru。kono影響de小竹向原 - Ikebukuro Station間ga17時過gimade運休suru。kono事故no影響wo重ku見ta国土交通省関東運輸局ha東京地下鉄ni対shite早期no原因究明to再発防止wo求meru警告文書wo発出shita。
 12月7日：2時10分goro、Toyosu Stationde夜間作業事故ga発生shi、死傷者ga出ru。kono影響de銀座一丁目駅 - 新木場駅間ga8時30分過gimade運休shi、銀座一丁目駅de折ri返shi運転ga行wareta。
 2012年（Heisei24年）
 3月17日：platformdoa設置工事no進捗ni伴i、小田急romansukano乗ri入rewo中止。
 9月10日：東急5050系4000番台no営業運転開始。当日ha東武東上線森林公園駅 - 新木場駅間no朝1往復運転。
 8月4日：新富町駅 - 新木場駅間de新CS-ATCno使用wo開始。有楽町線全線no新CS-ATC化wo完了。
 11月4日：小竹向原駅 - 千川駅間no立体交差化工事ni伴u線路工事notame、終日Wakōshi Station - Ikebukuro Station間de運休。

 2月7日：Edogawabashi Station - 新木場駅間de携帯電話no利用ga可能tonaru。

 3月21日：Wakōshi Station - 要町駅間de携帯電話no利用ga可能tonaru。
 12月7日：全駅noplatformdoano設置ga完了。
 2014年（Heisei26年）2月8日：千川駅denoplatformdoa稼働開始womote、全駅noplatformdoaga稼働。
 2015年（Heisei27年）3月28日：Wakōshi Station - 小竹向原間nowanman運転ga開始。
 2016年（Heisei28年）2月14日：千川駅 - 小竹向原駅間no有楽町線Wakōshi Station方面連絡線ga完成shi、始発kara運用ga開始sareru。
 2018年（Heisei30年）3月17日：新富町駅to日比谷線築地駅tono乗ri換e業務wo開始。
 2020年（Reiwa2年）6月6日：銀座一丁目駅to銀座線, 丸no内線, 日比谷線銀座駅tono乗ri換e業務wo開始。
 2021年（Reiwa3年）2月21日：17000系ga営業運転開始。
 2022年（Reiwa4年）
 1月28日：Toyosu Station - 住吉間約4.8 kmno鉄道事業許可wo国土交通大臣ni申請。
 3月28日：国土交通大臣gaToyosu Station - 住吉間約4.8 kmno第一種鉄道事業wo許可。
 8月6日：全線dewanman運転wo開始。

都市交通審議会答申第15号deToyosu Station - 亀有間 (14.7 km) ga追加saretakotowo受ke、営団地下鉄ha1982年（Showa57年）1月29日nikono区間no鉄道事業免許wo申請shiteiru。

1985年（Showa60年）7月11日no運輸政策審議会答申第7号nioite、第8号線ha、Toyosu Stationkara北he分岐suru路線ga住吉 - 四tsu木間de第11号線（半蔵門線）to線路wo共用shi常磐線亀有駅（saraniJR武蔵野線方面）he至ru路線ni変更sareteori、Toyosu Stationto半蔵門線住吉駅ha線路ga分岐dekiruyou2面4線no構造de建設sareteiru。

沿線自治体tonaru江東区, 墨田区, 葛飾区, 松戸市no3区1市（及bi東京都, 千葉県no1都1県）ha1986年（Showa61年）ni"地下鉄8, 11号線促進連絡協議会"wo組織shi、2007年, 2008年（Heisei19年, Heisei20年）ni実施shita調査no結果、同協議会ga推進suru8号線, 11号線no延伸計画nouchi、Toyosu Station - 住吉駅間（約5.2 km）karano段階的na整備wo要望suru方針wo示shi、早期事業化wo目指shita活動ga行wareteiru。uchi、江東区（当該先行区間唯一no沿線自治体）ha地下鉄8号線no建設oyobi関連付帯設備ni要suru経費ni充terutametoshite、"（仮称）江東区地下鉄8号線建設基金"wo設置shi、Heisei22年度（2010年度）予算ni5億円wo計上shita。mata、Toyosu Station市場wo受ke入reru条件nimonateirutoshite東京都nadoni早期no延伸実現wo強ku求meteiru。

tadashi、東京metoroha2009年（Heisei21年）度3月期no有価証券報告書nioite申請時kara事業環境no変化wo理由ni"整備主体tonarukotoha極mete困難"to事業化ni消極的na態度wo表明shiteita。

江東区ha2011年7月ni第三sekutawo設立shite整備wo担i、運営wo行u上下分離方式de整備shi、Toyosu Station - 東陽町間（枝川付近）、東陽町 - 住吉間（千田付近）ni新駅wo建設suru計画案womatometa。2012年8月現在、江東区, 東京都, 東京metoronadoto検討委員会wo作ri協議中de、2015年度madeno着工wo目指shiteita。

2021年ni国土交通省ga交通政策審議会鉄道部会内ni設keta"東京圏niokeru今後no地下鉄netowakunoari方等ni関suru小委員会"nioite東京metorono完全民営化（株式売却）to並行shite都心部, 品川地下鉄構想to共ni有楽町線no延伸計画ni触rerareteori、2021年7月8日行wareta第5回小委員会to、同年7月15日ni示sareta"東京圏niokeru今後no地下鉄netowakunoari方等nitsuite"答申nioite、同区間nitsuite東京metoroga主体tonate整備wo進merunoga適切datosuru素案wo示sutotomoni、国ya東京都ga建設費wo補助suru方向性wo示shita。

事業費ha2019年時点no試算de1560億円daga、建築資材ya人件費no高騰de膨ramu見込mitonari、事業費no4分no3wo国ya都ga支援shi、東京metorono借入金niha財政投融資wo充teru方針dearu。2022年1月8日niha、延伸ni向keta作業ga同年4月kara本格的ni始maru見通shininata。 2022年度ha地質調査ya環境影響評価nadowo行i、具体的na金額ha2021年度末ni決maruga、国to都de計十数億円no見通shitoshiteiru。国ha2022年度no予算案ni環境影響nadono調査wo補助suru費用wo計上shi、都mo新年度予算案ni同様no費用wo盛ri込mu方針dearu。東京metoroha2022年（Reiwa4年）1月28日niToyosu Station - 住吉間約4.8 kmno鉄道事業許可wo国土交通大臣ni申請shi、同年3月28日ni第一種鉄道事業no許可wo受keta。opened時期ha2030年代半bade、事業費ha2689億8200万円wo予定shiteiru。補助金ga1738億3200万円、財政投融資資金kara951億5000万円wo見込ndeiru。

新tana駅toshite、（仮称）枝川駅（Toyosu Stationstarting point1.250 km）、（仮称）東陽町駅（Toyosu Stationstarting point3.070 km）、（仮称）千石駅（Toyosu Stationstarting point4.180 km）no3駅wo設置suru。mata、東陽町ha同名no駅gaaru東西線no地下ni新駅ga作rare、乗換駅tonaru。運転間隔ha1時間atari日中de約8本、朝nopiku時de約12本wo予定shiteiru。本線heno乗ri入re本数ha今後検討surutoshi、半蔵門線乗ri入reha現時点deha検討sareteinai。

本路線ni係ru損益haopened14年目de単年度損益ga黒字転換、opened29年目ni累積損益ga黒字転換shi、累積損益収支haopened29年目ni黒字転換、累積資金収支haopened40年目ni黒字転換wo想定shiteiru。

住吉駅以遠nitsuiteha、八潮駅（tsukubaekusupuresu）, 越谷reikutaun駅（武蔵野線）wo経由suru形deno延伸mo検討sareteiru。現在notokoro構想段階deari、運輸政策審議会答申第18号deha"2015年madeni整備着手surukotoga適当dearu路線"to位置付keraretaga、決定hanasareteinai。
章节.Operations:
Wakōshi Stationkara東武東上線wo経由shite川越市駅（朝夕ha森林公園駅）made、小竹向原駅karaha西武有楽町線経由Ikebukuro Station線直通de小手指駅（朝, 夕no一部列車ha飯能駅）madesorezore相互乗ri入rewo行teiru。

有楽町線nomino運行tonaru列車ya東武東上線直通列車ha全区間各駅停車de運行sareteiruga、西武Ikebukuro Station線直通列車ha西武線内wo準急, 快速, 快速急行toshite運行suru列車gaari、kono場合ha小竹向原駅de種別変更wo行u。mata後述suruyouni2017年3月25日kara有料指定列車"S-TRAIN"ga運転開始sareta。有楽町線heha平日daiyanomi乗ri入re、小手指駅 - Toyosu Station間de朝ni所沢発Toyosu Station行ki2本, 夕方以降niToyosu Station発小手指行kiwo5本運転shiteiru。有楽町線内no途中停車駅haIidabashi Station, 有楽町駅no2駅de、Toyosu Station行ha降車専用、小手指行ha乗車専用tonari、西武線内nomiya有楽町線内nomino利用ha不可能dearu。

Wakōshi Station - 小竹向原駅間ha副都心線to線路, 駅施設wo共有shi、新木場駅発着no列車to渋谷方面（東急東横線, minatomirai線, 東急新横浜線, 相鉄線直通）no列車gatomoni運行sareteiru。

副都心線tono共用区間dearuWakōshi Station - 小竹向原間deha10両編成to8両編成no列車de運行sareteiruga、小竹向原 - 新木場間hasubete10両編成no列車de運行sareteiru。

平日朝norashu時noIkebukuro Station方面deha数多kuno列車ga運行sare、小竹向原駅de新木場方面to渋谷方面ni振ri分kerareteiru。

sono他、野球ya花火大会nadonoibento開催時ni運転sareru臨時列車gaaru（詳細ha"臨時列車"no項wo参照）。特ni、埼玉西武raionzu主催試合nado西武domudenoibento開催日niha西武有楽町線, Ikebukuro Station線西所沢駅経由狭山線西武球場前行ga運転sare、東京都心oyobi湾岸地区kara西武domumade乗ri換enashide移動surukotogadekiru。mata、katsuteha年間30日程度、小田急線直通no臨時特急ga運転sareteita（詳細ha"特急romansuka"beirizoto""no項wo参照）。

運用番号no末尾ha、東京地下鉄車gaS、東武車gaT、西武車gaMdearu。東武車ha西武no路線ni入線dekizu、西武車ha東武no路線ni入線dekinai。副都心線, 東横線, minatomirai線no10両編成列車to共通運用de、東京地下鉄車hamochiron、東武車to西武車nimo有楽町線nomino運用gaari、西武車moWakōshi Stationmade乗ri入reru。東京地下鉄車no一部運用niha東武東上線川越市方面oyobiWakōshi Station発no列車ga、新木場折ri返shi後ni西武Ikebukuro Station線石神井公園方面行no列車tonaru運用moari、sono逆no運用moaru。一方、有楽町線新木場発no列車gaWakōshi Station, 東上線川越市方面, Ikebukuro Station線石神井公園方面de折ri返shite副都心線, 東急東横線, minatomirai線元町, 中華街方面行tonaru運用moari（10両編成noplatform有効長no関係上、東横線, minatomirai線内ha急行以上no種別）、sono逆no運用moaru。運用番号ha東京地下鉄車(21S - 97S)ha奇数（tadashi、平日rashu時ha一部no列車ga偶数番号de運用sareta。/48S、52S）、東武車(01T - 23T)to西武車（02M - 38M及biS-TRAINni充当sareru40000系限定no50M - ）no偶数gaaru。

副都心線de運用sareru東急電鉄, 横浜高速鉄道, 相模鉄道no車両ha、daiya乱renado特別no場合wo除ki、有楽町線no小竹向原 - 新木場間niha入線shinai。
章节.運転本数: 参考notame、Wakōshi Station - 小竹向原no線路共用区間wo走ru副都心線no列車mo記載suru。
章节.和光市方面, 東武東上線直通:
朝, 夕方：2 - 4分間隔（1時間ni10 - 17往復）
 1時間ni東上線直通列車（川越市駅, 志木駅発着）ga6 - 8往復（朝no新木場方面行kito夕方noWakōshi Station方面行kiha共ni森林公園駅発着便moari）、Wakōshi Station発着列車ga4 - 11往復、新木場駅発着ga5 - 15往復。全列車各駅停車。
 日中：5 - 7分間隔（1時間ni6往復）
 1時間ni新木場駅 - 川越市駅間no列車ga2往復、新木場駅 - Wakōshi Station間no列車ga各4往復。
 早朝, 夜間：6 - 9分間隔

東武東上線直通列車ha志木駅（平日nomino設定）, 川越市駅, 森林公園駅発着ga運転sareteiru。日中no川越市駅発着列車ha、小竹向原駅de西武Ikebukuro Station線系統noFrainani連絡suru。mata同駅06分oyobi36分発no新木場行ki、29分oyobi59分発noWakōshi Station行kiha同駅de森林公園駅発着noFrainani連絡suru（緩急接続）。

一方線内運転no列車no大多数no列車haWakōshi Station - 新木場駅間no運転daga、一部列車ha新木場駅 - Ikebukuro Station間no運用gaaru。mata新木場駅 - 小竹向原駅間no列車ga設定sare、平日ha新木場行2本、土休日ha小竹向原行, 新木場行ga1本zutsuaru。2013年3月16日nodaiya改正deha平日朝niToyosu Station行kiga設定saretaga、2019年10月15日nodaiya修正madeni新木場行kini延長sare消滅shiteiru（詳細haToyosu Station#駅構造wo参照）。初電toshiteIchigaya Station発Wakōshi Station行ki、有楽町発新木場行kigaaru。終電toshite平日ni川越市始発（土休日haWakōshi Station始発）Ikebukuro Station行kiga1本aru。

東上線内de人身事故, 各種toraburunadoniyori直通運転wo見合waseta場合、subeteWakōshi Stationdeno折ri返shi運転tonaruga、sono逆moaru。mataIkebukuro Stationde運転wo取riyamerukotomoaru。
章节.西武有楽町線, 池袋線直通:
朝：6 - 9分間隔
 石神井公園駅, 保谷駅, 清瀬駅, 所沢駅, 小手指駅, 飯能駅発着、新木場行ki
 sono他no時間帯：5 - 30分間隔（1時間ni2 - 6往復）
 日中ha新木場駅 - 小手指駅間, 新木場駅 - 保谷駅間no列車tomoni1時間各2往復（計4往復）運行sareteiru。土休日ha保谷行ki一部ga清瀬発着ninateiru。2022年3月nodaiya改正de6往復kara4往復ni減便sareta。
 夕方以降ha新木場駅 - 石神井公園駅, 飯能駅間no設定moaru。
 ※西武domude野球ga開催sareru場合、西武球場前行kino列車mo運行sareru。
 

石神井公園駅、清瀬駅発着wo中心ni運転sare、所沢発着mo運転sareteiru。飯能発着hawazukani運転sareteiru。平日nomi清瀬発Toyosu Station行ki列車ga一時期存在shiteitaga、Wakōshi Station方面, 東武東上線直通no節de前述no通ri、現在ha設定sareteinai。

日中no小手指駅, 保谷駅発着各駅停車ha、小竹向原駅de、副都心線各駅停車, 東急東横線内急行noWakōshi Station発着列車（東武東上線森林公園駅発着noFrainano直前, 直後）ni連絡suru。

西武線内no種別ha各駅停車以外ni準急, 快速, 快速急行toshite運行sarerumonogaaru。列車種別hasubete小竹向原駅de変更sareru。

Ikebukuro Station線内deno人身事故, 各種toraburunadoniyori当路線tono直通運転wo見合waseta場合、西武線直通列車haIkebukuro Stationnite客扱iwo打chi切ri、小竹向原駅ni回送shita後ni新木場方面he折ri返su。
章节.各駅停車:
東京地下鉄線内no各駅ni停車suru種別。後述no準急廃止後mo、副都心線no急行ni対shiteno"各駅停車"no一tsuno系統toshitekono種別no表現ha残sareteiru。

有楽町線no種別表示ha車種ya所属会社niyote"各駅停車"to"各停"ga混在shiteiruga、前者no場合demo西武Ikebukuro Station線内deha"各停"表記ni切ri替erareru。

東上線内deha普通toshite案内sareruga、各停表示nomama運行sarerukotomoaru。konohokadaiya乱reno際niha、副都心線直通列車no運用変更nadoniyori東上線内急行, 快速急行toshite運転sareru場合moaru。

西武Ikebukuro Station線内ha各停以外ni小竹向原駅de種別wo変更shite快速, 準急, 快速急行toshite運行surumonogaaru。katsuteha新木場駅kara西武Ikebukuro Station線内no種別wo案内shiteita（正確niha各停ha西武有楽町線小竹向原駅kara普通deata）。一方新木場方面行ha西武有楽町線練馬駅kara全列車ga各駅ni停車surutame、練馬駅kara普通、小竹向原駅kara各停toshite案内sareteita。

2022年3月12日nodaiya改正de日中no西武線直通列車ha1時間6往復kara4往復ni減便sare、減便分no運行区間ga新木場駅 - Ikebukuro Station間tonatatame、日中demoIkebukuro Station行kiga設定sareta。
章节.副都心線no列車: 副都心線opened後、当路線noWakōshi Station - 小竹向原駅間ha副都心線tono共用区間tonateiru。kono区間niha副都心線no各駅停車, 通勤急行, 急行mo運転sareteiru。詳shikuha"副都心線"wo参照。
章节.副都心線開業ni伴u主na変化:
2008年6月14日no副都心線openedni伴i、併走区間, 線路共用区間noaru有楽町線demo大幅nadaiya改正ga行wareta。sono際no主na変化ha以下notooridearu。
 優等種別no"準急"ga設定sareta（詳細ha後述）。Wakōshi Station - 新木場駅間no所要時分ha各駅停車ha49分35秒、準急列車ha45分20秒tosareta。
 小竹向原駅de、有楽町線新木場行ki列車to副都心線渋谷行ki列車、Wakōshi Station方面行ki列車to西武線直通列車de相互接続ga行wareru。koreha、副都心線opened前kara新木場行ki列車to新線Ikebukuro Station行ki列車、Wakōshi Station方面行ki列車to西武線直通列車de相互接続ga行wareteita（tadashi副都心線opened前後tomo全便dehanai）。
 小竹向原駅de、片方no列車ga遅reta場合demo接続待chiha行wanakunata。sonotame接続予定no列車同士demo遅reta場合ha接続wo行wanai。副都心線opened前ha片方no列車ga遅reta場合接続待chiwo行teita。
 東武東上線mataha西武線tono相互直通列車de、Wakōshi Stationmataha小竹向原駅nite種別変更wo行umonoga増eta。
 西武線直通列車no始発, 終着駅no変更ya、系統入re替ega行wareta。以下hasono一例。
 各駅停車ha清瀬発着ga増eta。
 日中no新木場 - 飯能発着（快速）to新線Ikebukuro Station - 小手指間（各駅停車）wo入re替eru形de、新木場 - 小手指間（準急）to渋谷 - 飯能間（快速）ni変更sareta。
章节.過去ni存在shita種別:
特急romansuka"beirizoto" 

小田急電鉄所属no60000形"MSE"niyori小田急線to千代田線wo直通suru特急romansukano一部wo、"beirizoto"toshite年間30日程度、千代田線北千住駅kara当路線no新木場駅ni行ki先, 始発駅wo変更shite運転shiteita。

有楽町線Sakuradamon Stationto千代田線霞ke関駅間wo結bu連絡線（詳shikuha後述）wo経由shi、霞ke関駅de方向転換wo行u。有楽町線内dehaToyosu Stationto新木場駅nomini停車suru。

2011年9月25日以降運行wo休止shiteitaga、2012年3月17日nodaiya改正de運行中止tonata。
章节.準急:
相互乗ri入re先deno種別toiukotodehanaku、有楽町線内de通過駅noaru列車toshite初mete設定sareta種別。2008年6月14日nodaiya改正de、平日no昼間to、土休日no早朝, 深夜wo除ku時間帯ni設定sareta。併走区間gaaru副都心線急行, 通勤急行totomoni、東京no地下鉄deno料金不要no優等列車no運転ha、東西線快速、都営新宿線急行、都営浅草線eapoto快特ni次ide4例目deata。

停車駅haWakōshi Station、小竹向原、Ikebukuro Station - 新木場間no各駅deata。

imejikaraha黄緑。

設定当初ha東武東上線oyobi西武線tono相互直通運転wosuru列車mo存在shita。運転本数ha新木場方面ha毎時3本（Wakōshi Station発2本、小手指発1本）、Wakōshi Station, 東上線系統to西武線系統ha毎時各2本zutsude、土休日daiyadeha21時頃made運転sare、平日de往復22本（土休日ha往復44本）ga運行sareteita。shikashi、同年11月29日nodaiya改正de平日, 土休日daiyatomo日中nomi、両方向tomo毎時2本（1日atari10往復）ni大幅減便shita上desubeteno準急gaWakōshi Station - 新木場間no線内運転nomitonari、東武東上線, 西武線直通準急ya夕方以降no準急ha各駅停車ni格下gesareta。sarani、準急no運行niyote要町駅, 千川駅deha停車列車no本数, 乗客no利用機会ga減少shitatame、2駅ga所在suru豊島区議会ha準急全廃wo求meru意見書wo出shiteita。koushita意見wo受ke、東京metoroha2010年3月6日nodaiya改正de準急wo廃止surukotowo発表shi、有楽町線no準急ha登場kara2年足razude姿wo消shita。

東上線直通no準急haWakōshi Stationde"普通"ni種別変更no上、東上線内wo普通列車toshite運行shiteita（東上線準急to停車駅ga変waranainode、7000系no一部車両ha"準急"nomama走raseru場合moata。mata、東武車両nofurukaraLED表示ha有楽町線準急ga緑色、東上線準急ga青色deata）。tadashi、東上線直通no準急ha本数ga少naku、平日ha新木場→川越市no片道1本ga運転sarerunomi、土休日mo朝no川越市→新木場no3本to夕方以降no5往復ga運転sarerunomide、土休日ni1本森林公園行kigaaru以外hasubete川越市発着deata。一方、西武線直通no準急ha西武線内demo"準急"toshite運行surumonoto、小竹向原de"各停""快速"ni種別変更wo行umonogaata。mata、西武線直通no準急ha小手指発着wo中心ni本数ga多ku、一部列車ha清瀬発着, 飯能発着toshite運行sareteita。

英文.全文:
The Yurakucho Line (有楽町線, Yūrakuchō-sen) is a railway line operated by Tokyo Metro (東京地下鉄) that connects Wakōshi Station in Wakō, Saitama with Shinkiba Station in Kōtō, Tokyo. In the Urban Transport Council's route numbering, the section between Kotake-mukaihara and Shinkiba is Line 8, and the section between Wakōshi and Kotake-mukaihara is Line 13; however, in the Railway Directory (鉄道要覧) published under the supervision of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, the Wakōshi–Shinkiba section is listed as Line 8, Yurakucho Line.
The line takes its name from the fact that it passes through Yūrakuchō (see also the relevant section below). The line color used on the rolling stock, route maps, and transfer guidance is "gold" (#c1a470), and the route symbol is Y.

Overview
The Yurakucho Line runs roughly from northwest to southeast through the heart of Tokyo. Taking the A-destination trains (toward Shinkiba) as the reference, the line runs generally southeastward from Wakōshi through Kotake-mukaihara, Ikebukuro, and Iidabashi; from Iidabashi to Ichigaya it turns temporarily southwest, following alongside the Namboku Line and the JR Chūō–Sōbu Local Line; from Ichigaya it turns back southeast, proceeding straight through Nagatachō, Yūrakuchō, and Toyosu to the terminus at Shinkiba.
Leaving Wakōshi Station, trains climb a 35‰ gradient, cross over the down tracks of the Tōbu Tōjō Line, and run parallel to them for a while. Crossing the prefectural border, the line dives underground just before approaching Narimasu Station on the Tōjō Line, arriving at Chikatetsu Narimasu Station. It runs parallel to the Tōjō Line as far as Chikatetsu Akatsuka and Shimo-Akatsuka stations, then leaves it. After merging with the Seibu Yūrakuchō Line, trains arrive at Kotake-mukaihara Station; about 560 m after departure the Fukutoshin Line branches off, and up to Ikebukuro the line forms track-separated quadruple track directly beneath the Yurakucho Line, dividing at Ikebukuro into routes toward Shinkiba and toward Shibuya.
Underground sections are constructed mainly by the cut-and-cover method with a double-track structure, but the section shared with the Fukutoshin Line noted above is a two-level stacked tunnel, and Kōjimachi Station and Ginza-itchōme Station are two-level structures because the roads above are narrow. The line adopted shield tunneling (single- and double-track tunnels) on a large scale, and Nagatachō Station was constructed using the station shield method. Particularly in Kōjimachi, Chiyoda, the line passes directly beneath the Mitsubishi Bank (now MUFG Bank) Kōjimachi Branch; because the building's foundation piles would obstruct the tunnel, a large-scale project was required, underpinning a nine-story building with a total weight of 10,600 tonnes so that the subway tunnel could be built beneath it (the building was rebuilt in February 2004 and is now the Kōjimachi Diamond Building).
In addition, leaving Tatsumi Station, the line climbs a steep 33–34.5‰ gradient to street level (an elevated section), runs parallel to the Tokyo Waterfront Area Rapid Transit (TWR) Rinkai Line, and reaches its terminus at Shinkiba Station where the JR Keiyō Line merges on the direct overhead alignment. The roughly 25 km continuous tunnel section between the vicinity of Chikatetsu Narimasu and the vicinity of Tatsumi is the longest on the Tokyo Metro network.
The underground stations from Tsukishima to Tatsumi are close to Tokyo Bay, and as a countermeasure against flooding from storm surges and similar events, steel floodgates have been installed at the station passageways. Waterproof doors that close the entire cross-section of the tunnel have been installed on the Tsukishima side of Shintomichō and between Tatsumi and Shinkiba. These are normally stowed in a machinery room at the top of the tunnel, and in an emergency they are lowered to prevent water from entering the tunnel.

Urban Transport Council Report No. 6
Report No. 6 of the Urban Transport Council, issued on June 8, 1962 (Shōwa 37), planned subways beyond Line 6 onward, and the then-Line 10 was defined as a route "from the Nakanoshima direction via Mejiro, Iidabashi, and Asakusabashi to the direction of Kinshichō." Based on this report, Ministry of Construction Notification No. 2187, promulgated on August 29 of the same year, formally established the report's Line 10 as Urban Planning Line 8: "Nakamura-bashi Station – Ekoda – Nishi-Ochiai – Shiinamachi – Mejiro Station – Edogawa-bashi – Iidabashi Station – Jinbōchō – Sudachō – Higashi-Ryōgoku Midorichō – Kinshichō Station" (17.5 km).
In response to this decision, the Teito Rapid Transit Authority (Eidan) applied on October 16, 1962 (Shōwa 37) for a local railway construction license for Line 8, Yahara – Kōtōbashi, together with Line 7 (the Namboku Line), for which urban planning had been decided at the same time. The line was proposed as Line 8, Yahara–Kōtōbashi (20.88 km, extending slightly west from Nakamura-bashi in the urban plan). The Tokyo Metropolitan Government (Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation) subsequently applied for licenses for both lines as well, resulting in competing applications.

Urban Transport Council Report No. 10
Report No. 10 of the Urban Transport Council, issued on April 10, 1968 (Shōwa 43), revised Line 8 to a route "from the Narimasu and Nerima directions via Mukaihara and Ikebukuro, and also from the Nakamura-bashi direction via Mejiro, passing Gokokuji, Iidabashi, Ichigaya, Nagatachō, Yūrakuchō, and Ginza, to the direction of Akashi-chō," and stated: "Furthermore, with regard to the section between Nakamura-bashi and Gokokuji within this route, extensions from Nakamura-bashi and Gokokuji are to be studied in the future, taking into account transport demand, housing development, etc."
Based on this report, Ministry of Construction Notification No. 3731, promulgated on December 28 of the same year, incorporated the Narimasu–Ikebukuro section, formerly part of Line 4 (Marunouchi Line), into Line 8, and Line 8, formerly running from Nakamura-bashi to Kinshichō, was substantially revised into "a main line between Nerima and Ginza (16.5 km), a branch between Narimasu and Kotake-chō (6.3 km), and a branch between Nakamura-bashi and Otowa (9.1 km)."
Of the Line 8 in Report No. 6 of the Urban Transport Council noted earlier, the Nakamura-bashi – Mejiro Station – Iidabashi Station section was re-routed and incorporated into new Line 8 (the Yurakucho Line), while the Iidabashi Station – Kinshichō Station section was re-routed and incorporated into Line 10 (the Toei Shinjuku Line).
In response to this change, the Teito Rapid Transit Authority applied on June 6, 1968 (Shōwa 43) for a local railway construction license for Line 8 between Mukaihara and Narimasu-chō and between Nishi-Ikebukuro and Akashi-chō, and also applied for approval to revise the business plan for the Ikebukuro–Mukaihara section for which it held a license as Line 4 (Marunouchi Line). On July 22 of the same year, it applied for a local railway construction license for the Kami-Saginomiya–Otowa section (Nakamura-bashi–Gokokuji), and at the same time submitted a request to withdraw the pending license application for the Yahara–Kōtōbashi section. The June 6 license application and business plan revision application were granted and approved on October 30 of the same year, and the withdrawal of the license was accepted on August 13. The license application for the Kami-Saginomiya–Otowa section (Nakamura-bashi–Gokokuji) was withdrawn on October 23, 1973 (Shōwa 48).
At the time of applying for the Line 8 (Yurakucho Line) license, the Ikebukuro–Akashi-chō (now Shintomichō) section was scheduled to open in March 1973 (Shōwa 48) and the Narimasu (now Chikatetsu Narimasu)–Ikebukuro section in March 1974 (Shōwa 49). Of Line 8 (Yurakucho Line), the Nerima–Mukaihara (now Kotake-mukaihara) section was to be constructed by Seibu Railway, with through operation between the Eidan Yurakucho Line and the Seibu Ikebukuro Line planned.
On September 5, 1968 (Shōwa 43), the Teito Rapid Transit Authority and Seibu Railway exchanged a memorandum regarding through operation, with the start of through operation between the Eidan Yurakucho Line and the Seibu Ikebukuro Line targeted for 1973 (Shōwa 48). In reality, full through operation between the Seibu Ikebukuro Line and the Eidan Yurakucho Line did not begin until 25 years later, in 1998 (Heisei 10).
After obtaining the route license, the Teito Rapid Transit Authority proceeded with procedures toward construction, but land acquisition proved difficult particularly in Kita-machi, Nerima Ward (near Chikatetsu Akatsuka–Heiwadai), and coordination with the above-ground Radial Route No. 36 between Heiwadai and Kanamechō delayed the start of construction (see below).
When the Yurakucho Line was first planned in 1968 (Shōwa 43), the depot had been planned near Narimasu; however, since the surrounding area had already been developed as a residential district and land acquisition was expected to be difficult, land located between Wakōshi Station and Asaka Station was acquired, and a depot (the present Wakō Depot) was established near Wakōshi. In addition, the section between Wakō Depot and Eidan Narimasu had been planned as a siding (return line) for the depot, but local residents and others strongly requested that it be operated as a revenue-earning line.

Urban Transport Council Report No. 15
Report No. 15 of the Urban Transport Council, issued on March 1, 1972 (Shōwa 47), changed the origin side of Line 8 from Nakamura-bashi to Hōya, and added, on the terminus side, the sections Akashi-chō–Wangan and Toyosu–Tōyōchō–Sumiyoshi-chō–Oshiage–Kameari. The report also indicated that the Hōya–Nerima section would have the Seibu Ikebukuro Line quadruple-tracked, the Nakamura-bashi–Gokokuji section was deleted, the Gokokuji–Mejiro section was incorporated into Tokyo Planned Line 12, and the Shiki–Mukaihara section was separated as Tokyo Planned Line 13.
Of these, the Kotake-mukaihara–Shinkiba section opened as the Yurakucho Line, the Nerima–Kotake-mukaihara section as the Seibu Yūrakuchō Line, and the Shakujii-kōen–Nerima section as an additional Seibu Ikebukuro Line track (quadruple-tracking). On the terminus side, extension had been planned along the Wangan waterfront between the Keiyō area and a seaside new town, but because the Keiyō Line—which had been planned along an almost identical route—was at the time being planned as a freight-only line and was later converted to passenger service, the Yurakucho Line's plans were curtailed at Shinkiba.
The branch line between Nakamura-bashi–Mejiro–Gokokuji (9.6 km) that had been deleted in Report No. 15 was the subject of an urban planning decision along a route following Shinobazu-dōri, Mejiro-dōri, and Senkawa-dōri, and remains valid to this day; however, as noted above, the route license had been withdrawn at the application stage, and the section incorporated as a branch of Tokyo Planned Line 12 (Toei Ōedo Line) was not licensed by the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation and was deleted in Transport Policy Council Report No. 7 of 1985 (Shōwa 60), so the plan has effectively been abandoned. The Gokokuji Station for this branch was planned as a separate station facility from the present-day Yurakucho Line, with no through connection contemplated.

Line 13 and Construction Delays
On the other hand, in Report No. 15 noted above, the new Tokyo Planned Line 13 was announced as a route "from Shiki through Wakōshi, Narimasu, Mukaihara, Ikebukuro, Higashi-Ikebukuro, Mejiro-higashi, Suwachō, and Nishi-Ōkubo to Shinjuku," with the note that "extensions from Shinjuku via Shibuya and Shinagawa toward Haneda should also be studied." The report indicated that the Shiki–Wakōshi section would have the Tōbu Tōjō Line quadruple-tracked.
The Narimasu–Kotake-mukaihara section already under construction as Line 8 (Yurakucho Line) was incorporated into part of Line 13, and the Kotake-mukaihara–Ikebukuro section was designated as a shared alignment of Lines 8 and 13, but construction of this section by the Teito Rapid Transit Authority was imminent. Accordingly, following discussions with the Ministry of Transport (as it was then), the Kotake-mukaihara–Ikebukuro section was treated as a change of construction method with quadruple track, and a route license was sought for the Wakōshi–Narimasu section pursuant to Report No. 15. From fiscal 1975 onward, construction funding was budgeted under the Wakōshi–Akashi-chō (later Shinkiba) section without distinction between Lines 8 and 13.
With the establishment of Line 13, the Teito Rapid Transit Authority negotiated with Seibu Railway and Tōbu Railway, and in August 1975 (Shōwa 50) exchanged the following memorandum regarding through operation between Lines 8 and 13.
The Wakōshi–Ikebukuro section of Line 13 (→Shin-Ikebukuro→Fukutoshin Line Ikebukuro), the Kotake-mukaihara–Ikebukuro section of Line 8 (Yurakucho Line), and the Nerima–Kotake-mukaihara section of the Seibu Yūrakuchō Line are premised on simultaneous opening.
Kotake-mukaihara Station is to be configured so that Line 8 and Line 13 trains can run through onto each other.
The service pattern is to be based on Urban Transport Council Report No. 15.
Line 13 will operate between the Tōbu Tōjō Line–Wakōshi–Ikebukuro (→Shin-Ikebukuro→Fukutoshin Line Ikebukuro), and Line 8 between the Seibu Ikebukuro Line–Nerima–Kotake-mukaihara–the Yurakucho Line toward Shintomichō, with roughly six trains per hour running through from Line 13 onto Line 8 (Yurakucho Line) during rush hours. In the future, through operation is to alternate between Lines 13 and 8 to the extent that it does not interfere with timetabling.
This was because the Teito Rapid Transit Authority had commenced construction of the Narimasu–Kotake-mukaihara section as Line 8 and obtained the cooperation of local residents by advertising "direct service to Ginza," making it necessary to operate trains from the Wakōshi direction toward the Yurakucho Line. However, due to problems with land purchase and construction consent from local residents, construction was significantly delayed, and use of the Line 13 facilities between Kotake-mukaihara and Ikebukuro was deferred for the time being.
In addition, aligned with the Tōbu Tōjō Line's plan to quadruple-track the Shiki–Wakōshi section, the Teito Rapid Transit Authority decided on through operation between the Tōbu Tōjō Line and Line 13 via Wakōshi Station, and to operate the Wakōshi–Eidan Narimasu section as a revenue line, changing its application accordingly to a local railway construction license. Construction of the Wakōshi–Eidan Narimasu section began in September 1978 (Shōwa 53); at that point, opening of the Wakōshi–Ikebukuro section was scheduled for September 1981 (Shōwa 56), but delays in land purchase near Wakōshi Station pushed the opening back to autumn 1987 (Shōwa 62).
From the perspective of Urban Transport Council Report No. 15, the Wakōshi–Ikebukuro section is "Line 13" (the present Fukutoshin Line), a line distinct from the Yurakucho Line; however, because this section is operated as an integrated service with the Yurakucho Line between Ikebukuro and Shintomichō, and to avoid passenger confusion, the Wakōshi–Ikebukuro section also came to be called the "Yurakucho Line."
Of these, the Wakōshi–Kotake-mukaihara section opened as part of the Yurakucho Line, and the Shiki–Wakōshi section as additional Tōbu Tōjō Line quadruple track. In addition, the Line 13 section between Kotake-mukaihara and Ikebukuro (→Shin-Ikebukuro) opened in December 1994 as the Yurakucho New Line (now the Fukutoshin Line).
Because Kotake-mukaihara Station is the junction with the Seibu Yūrakuchō Line, it has a two-platform, four-track structure; on the Ikebukuro side, a six-track section long enough for a 10-car train plus margin was installed so that Line 13 trains from the Wakōshi direction and Line 8 trains from the Nerima direction could both run through in either direction.
The Kotake-mukaihara–Ikebukuro section is an integrated structure with the Line 8 and Line 13 tunnels stacked one above the other. This is because constructing the Line 13 tunnel anew after Line 8 had opened would be difficult, and a stacked tunnel structure is economical; moreover, running the Line 8 and Line 13 tunnels in parallel was constrained by the width of the roads above, so the stacked-tunnel structure, which conserves land, was adopted. At Senkawa and Kanamechō stations, the second basement level serves as the Line 8 (Yurakucho Line) platforms and the third basement level as the Line 13 (Fukutoshin Line) platforms; when the Yurakucho Line opened in 1983 (Shōwa 58), only the second-basement portion entered service.
Of the Line 8 section between Narimasu and Ikebukuro, the sections other than those under Kawagoe Road (National Route 254) (near Chikatetsu Narimasu–Chikatetsu Akatsuka) conflicted with the planned roads of Tokyo's Radial Route No. 35, Radial Route No. 36, and Auxiliary Street Route No. 78 (Auxiliary Route No. 78), and Radial Route No. 36 in particular faced strong opposition from local residents, so difficult land negotiations had been anticipated from the outset. The section under Kawagoe Road (National Route 254) began construction in February 1972 (Shōwa 47) and was completed in March 1975 (Shōwa 50); however, because the opening of the preceding and following sections was significantly delayed, the facilities remained unused for eight years. However, since they were completed before the inflation triggered by the oil shock, this ultimately held down construction costs.
Between Heiwadai and Ikebukuro, the Tokyo street project (urban planning road) and subway construction had originally been planned as simultaneous works. However, in the Hikawadai–Senkawa section, where no road existed and one would have to be newly developed, local residents strongly opposed the planned road, concerned about exhaust fumes and noise, drawing the road plan into the subway construction and making land negotiations difficult. That said, many residents were in favor of the subway construction. Ultimately, the oil shock sharply worsened Tokyo's finances, making road development difficult, so in September 1975 (Shōwa 50) the Teito Rapid Transit Authority changed its plans to construct the subway first, with the Tokyo planned road to be developed anew after subway construction.

About this line
One of the purposes of construction was to relieve congestion on the Marunouchi Line, which had limited scope for increasing transport capacity because of its smaller car gauge and shorter trains. Because transferring at Ikebukuro was convenient, it contributed greatly to relieving congestion, much as the Chiyoda Line did for the Hibiya Line.
In addition, in anticipation of the opening of the Ginza-itchōme–Ikebukuro section in 1974 (Shōwa 49), four automatic ticket gates were installed at Ikebukuro Station and two at Ginza-itchōme Station, following those at Nakano-sakaue on the Marunouchi Line and Ebisu on the Hibiya Line. This was because the section had no in-station transfers to other lines, making it well suited as a pilot section for gate automation. Automatic ticket gates were not installed at stations other than the two terminal stations, Ikebukuro and Ginza-itchōme; however, magnetic tickets were sold at all stations on the Yurakucho Line, and exit with ordinary tickets was also supported. However, as magnetic ticketing had not yet gained traction on other lines at the time, efficient operation was not achieved, and the gates were removed for a time when the line was extended to Eidan Narimasu (now Chikatetsu Narimasu), with the experiment ending in failure. In other respects, the passenger guidance sign system introduced at Ōtemachi was adopted in full.
As for Line 13, the route from Shin-Ikebukuro via Nishi-Waseda and Shinjuku-sanchōme to Shibuya opened on June 14, 2008 (Heisei 20) as the Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line. In addition, from March 16, 2013 (Heisei 25), the Fukutoshin Line began through service from Shibuya via the Tōkyū Tōyoko Line to Minatomirai Line Motomachi-Chūkagai Station. As a future development plan, Line 8 is planned to extend from Toyosu Station, branching to Noda-shi Station (for details, see the section "Metropolitan High-Speed Railway Line 8 Extension Plan"). The Teito Rapid Transit Authority had applied for a local railway business license for the Toyosu–Kameari section (14.7 km) on January 29, 1982 (Shōwa 57), but no license was granted. Under the Eidan plan, construction was scheduled from fiscal 1985 to fiscal 1992, with construction costs estimated at ¥272.0 billion. Subsequently, in 2022 (Reiwa 4), Tokyo Metro applied for a railway business license for the Toyosu–Sumiyoshi section, which was granted by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism that year.
The Yurakucho Line was the first Tokyo subway line to be extended into Saitama Prefecture. Apart from the Fukutoshin Line, which shares a section with this line, the only Tokyo subway lines extending beyond Tokyo's 23 wards are the Yurakucho Line and the Tōzai Line; including the Toei Subway, only three lines in all of Tokyo's subway network qualify, the third being the Toei Shinjuku Line.

Line data
Operating distance: 28.3 km (of which above-ground sections: 2.3 km)
Track gauge: 1,067 mm
Number of stations: 24 (including the termini)
Double-track sections: Entire line (the 3.2 km between Kotake-mukaihara and Ikebukuro is track-separated quadruple track shared with the Fukutoshin Line)
Electrified sections: Entire line (1,500 V DC overhead catenary)
Block system: Speed-control type (New CS-ATC)
Because the Yurakucho Line was extended in stages, the switch from the conventional CS-ATC system to New CS-ATC was implemented in three separate sections. Line name
The name "Yurakucho Line" was chosen through a public contest held between November 1 and December 15, 1973 (Shōwa 48), attracting 30,591 submissions proposing 2,519 distinct names.
The top vote-getter was "Kōjimachi Line." However, the character 麹 was not among the then-tōyō kanji and was considered difficult and unfamiliar, while many entries proposed names related to "Yūrakuchō," including second-place "Yurakucho Line" and fifth-place "Yūraku Line"; moreover, extension to the Wangan area was planned (at the time of selection), which would place Yūrakuchō in the middle of the line after the extension opened. Accordingly, on January 9, 1974 (Shōwa 49), the line was named the "Yurakucho Line."
Among the submissions was reportedly also "Kangaroo Line" (a play on the association of "袋" with marsupials).

Construction costs
The total construction cost of the line between Wakōshi and Shinkiba (not including the section built as the Yurakucho New Line) was ¥492.0 billion. The breakdown is as follows: civil engineering costs of ¥296.150328 billion, electrical costs of ¥44.826812 billion, rolling stock costs of ¥65.859654 billion, and other costs of ¥85.163206 billion.

Track structure
Apart from Japanese National Railways (JNR, as it was then), the line was the first among private and subway railways in Japan to adopt 60 kg rail (on the main line). The adoption of 60 kg rail increased rail strength by a factor of 1.5 and extended service life by 4–6 years. While underground sections had conventionally used direct-fixation track, vibration and noise from it were significant, so the line newly adopted a "vibration-damping sleeper structure" (near private land). Initially, rubber pads were placed between the rails and sleepers, and the sleepers were covered with vibration-damping rubber; after the opening of Shintomichō, a new structure was adopted in which a vibration-damping device comprising damping rubber, damping pads, and damping cushions was laid under the rail supports, with the space beneath the rails left hollow. On ballasted track sections, vibration-damping mats or sheets were laid under the track, all proving highly effective in reducing vibration and noise.

In response to the addition of the Toyosu–Kameari section (14.7 km) in Urban Transport Council Report No. 15, the Teito Rapid Transit Authority applied for a railway business license for this section on January 29, 1982 (Shōwa 57).
In Transport Policy Council Report No. 7 of July 11, 1985 (Shōwa 60), Line 8 was revised to a route branching north from Toyosu, sharing track with Line 11 (Hanzōmon Line) between Sumiyoshi and Yotsugi and continuing to Jōban Line Kameari Station (and onward toward the JR Musashino Line); Toyosu Station on the Yurakucho Line and Sumiyoshi Station on the Hanzōmon Line were built with two-platform, four-track structures permitting the tracks to diverge.
The three wards and one city along the route—Kōtō, Sumida, and Katsushika wards and Matsudo City (plus Tokyo and Chiba prefectures)—organized the "Subway Lines 8 and 11 Promotion Council" in 1986 (Shōwa 61). Based on surveys conducted in 2007 and 2008 (Heisei 19 and Heisei 20), the council indicated a policy of requesting staged development beginning with the Toyosu–Sumiyoshi section (approximately 5.2 km) of the Line 8 and Line 11 extension plans it promotes, and activities were carried out aiming at early commercialization. Of these, Kōtō Ward (the only municipality along the priority section) established the "(tentatively named) Kōtō Ward Subway Line 8 Construction Fund" to cover the costs of constructing Subway Line 8 and associated ancillary facilities, and allocated ¥500 million in the fiscal 2010 (Heisei 22) budget. It has also pressed Tokyo and others for early extension as a condition of accepting the Toyosu Market.
However, in its securities report for the fiscal year ending March 2009 (Heisei 21), Tokyo Metro, citing changes in the business environment since the application, stated that "becoming the developing entity would be extremely difficult," reflecting a passive attitude toward commercialization.
In July 2011, Kōtō Ward established a third-sector company to undertake development, planning an upper-and-lower-structure separation model in which the company handles construction and operations, with new stations to be built in the Toyosu–Tōyōchō section (near Edagawa) and the Tōyōchō–Sumiyoshi section (near Chikada). As of August 2012, deliberations were under way with a study committee formed with Kōtō Ward, the Tokyo Metropolitan Government, Tokyo Metro, and others, targeting the start of construction by fiscal 2015.
In the "Subcommittee on the Future of the Subway Network in the Tokyo Area," established within the Railway Subcommittee of the Transport Policy Council by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism in 2021, the Yurakucho Line extension was discussed alongside the metropolitan core and Shinagawa subway concept, in parallel with the full privatization (sale of shares) of Tokyo Metro. At the fifth meeting of the subcommittee held on July 8, 2021, and in the draft report "On the Future of the Subway Network in the Tokyo Area" presented on July 15 of the same year, a draft was presented indicating that Tokyo Metro should take the lead in developing this section, along with a direction in which the national government and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government would subsidize construction costs.
Project costs were estimated at ¥156.0 billion as of 2019, but rising construction material and labor costs are expected to inflate the figure; the policy is for the national government and the metropolitan government to support three-quarters of the project cost, with fiscal investment and lending applied to Tokyo Metro's borrowings. On January 8, 2022, preparations for the extension were projected to begin in earnest from April of that year. In fiscal 2022, geological surveys and environmental impact assessments would be carried out, with the specific amount to be determined by the end of fiscal 2021; the national government and the metropolitan government projected a combined total of several billion yen. The national government included subsidies for environmental impact surveys and similar studies in its fiscal 2022 budget, and the metropolitan government planned to include similar expenses in its new fiscal year budget. Tokyo Metro applied for a railway business license for the approximately 4.8 km Toyosu–Sumiyoshi section to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism on January 28, 2022 (Reiwa 4), and obtained a Type 1 railway business license on March 28 of that year. Opening is planned for the mid-2030s, with project costs of ¥268.982 billion. Subsidies of ¥173.832 billion and ¥95.15 billion from fiscal investment and loan funds are projected.
Three new stations are planned: (tentatively named) Edagawa Station (1.250 km from Toyosu), (tentatively named) Tōyōchō Station (3.070 km from Toyosu), and (tentatively named) Sengoku Station (4.180 km from Toyosu). In addition, Tōyōchō Station will be built beneath the Tōzai Line station of the same name, becoming an interchange. Train frequency is planned at approximately 8 trains per hour during the day and approximately 12 per hour during the morning peak. The number of trains running through onto the main line is to be considered going forward, with through service onto the Hanzōmon Line not under consideration at this time.
Profitability for the line is projected to turn to single-year profit in the 14th year after opening, with cumulative profit, cumulative profit-and-loss, and cumulative cash flow turning positive in the 29th, 29th, and 40th years after opening respectively.
Beyond Sumiyoshi Station, extension via Yashio Station (Tsukuba Express) and Koshigaya Lake Town Station (Musashino Line) is also under study. This remains at the concept stage; in Transport Policy Council Report No. 18, the section was positioned as a route "for which commencement of development by 2015 is considered appropriate," but no decision has been made.

Service patterns
From Wakōshi Station, trains run through onto the Tōbu Tōjō Line as far as Kawagoe-shi Station (Shinrin-kōen in the morning and evening), and from Kotake-mukaihara Station through the Seibu Yūrakuchō Line onto the Seibu Ikebukuro Line as far as Kotesashi Station (some early-morning and evening trains as far as Hanno Station).
Services operating only on the Yurakucho Line and through services from the Tōbu Tōjō Line stop at all stations, while some through services from the Seibu Ikebukuro Line operate as Semi Express, Rapid, or Rapid Express within the Seibu network, with a change of service type at Kotake-mukaihara Station. In addition, as noted below, the paid reserved-seat service "S-TRAIN" began on March 25, 2017. S-TRAIN services enter the Yurakucho Line on weekdays only, running two morning trains from Tokorozawa to Toyosu and five evening Toyosu-to-Kotesashi trains. Within the Yurakucho Line, the only intermediate stops are Iidabashi and Yūrakuchō; Toyosu-bound trains are alighting-only and Kotesashi-bound trains boarding-only, and use solely within the Seibu or Yurakucho lines is not permitted.
The Wakōshi–Kotake-mukaihara section shares tracks and station facilities with the Fukutoshin Line, with trains to and from Shinkiba and Shibuya (through to the Tōkyū Tōyoko Line, Minatomirai Line, Tōkyū Shin-Yokohama Line, and Sagami Railway) both in operation.
On the shared Fukutoshin Line section between Wakōshi and Kotake-mukaihara, 10-car and 8-car trains operate, but all trains between Kotake-mukaihara and Shinkiba are 10-car formations.
During weekday morning rush hours, numerous trains operate toward Ikebukuro, divided at Kotake-mukaihara between Shinkiba-bound and Shibuya-bound services.
In addition, special trains operate for events such as baseball games and fireworks displays (see the "Special trains" section). In particular, on days when events are held at the Seibu Dome, such as Saitama Seibu Lions home games, services run to Seibu-Kyūjō-mae on the Seibu Sayama Line via the Seibu Yūrakuchō Line and Nishi-Tokorozawa on the Seibu Ikebukuro Line, allowing direct travel from central Tokyo and the waterfront district to the Seibu Dome without transfers. In the past, temporary limited expresses through to the Odakyū Line also ran on roughly 30 days per year (see the "Romancecar Bay Resort" section).
The last digit of the service number is S for Tokyo Metro trains, T for Tōbu trains, and M for Seibu trains. Tōbu trains cannot enter Seibu Railway tracks, and Seibu trains cannot enter Tōbu tracks. They operate in common with 10-car Fukutoshin Line, Tōyoko Line, and Minatomirai Line services, and not only Tokyo Metro but also Tōbu and Seibu trains have Yurakucho Line-only workings, with Seibu trains also running through to Wakōshi. Some Tokyo Metro workings run from the Tōbu Tōjō Line toward Kawagoe-shi or from Wakōshi, then after turning back at Shinkiba continue as services toward Shakujii-kōen on the Seibu Ikebukuro Line, with the reverse pattern also seen. Conversely, some workings depart Shinkiba on the Yurakucho Line and, after turning back at Wakōshi or on the Tōjō Line toward Kawagoe-shi or the Ikebukuro Line toward Shakujii-kōen, become services toward Motomachi-Chūkagai on the Fukutoshin Line, Tōkyū Tōyoko Line, and Minatomirai Line (operating as Express or faster within the Tōyoko and Minatomirai lines due to 10-car platform lengths), with the reverse pattern also seen. Tokyo Metro service numbers (21S–97S) are odd (although some trains use even numbers during weekday rush hours: /48S, 52S), while Tōbu (01T–23T) and Seibu (02M–38M, and 50M– reserved for 40000 series trains used on S-TRAIN) have even numbers.
Tōkyū Corporation, Yokohama Minatomirai Railway, and Sagami Railway trains used on the Fukutoshin Line do not enter the Yurakucho Line between Kotake-mukaihara and Shinkiba except in exceptional circumstances such as major disruption.

Local (all stations)
The service type calling at all stations within the Tokyo Metro network. Even after the abolition of the Semi Express (see below), this designation is retained as one category of "local" service in contrast to Fukutoshin Line Express services.
Service-type designations on the Yurakucho Line vary between "Local" (各駅停車) and "All-stations" (各停) depending on rolling stock and operator, but even where the former is used, the display switches to "All-stations" within the Seibu Ikebukuro Line.
Within the Tōjō Line, trains are announced as "Local" (普通), but some also operate with the all-stations display. In addition, during disruption, trains may operate as Express or Rapid Express within the Tōjō Line due to service reworkings of Fukutoshin Line through trains.
Within the Seibu Ikebukuro Line, apart from all-stations services, some trains change type at Kotake-mukaihara and operate as Rapid, Semi Express, or Rapid Express. In the past, Seibu Ikebukuro Line service types were announced from Shinkiba (strictly speaking, all-stations services were "Local" from Kotake-mukaihara on the Seibu Yūrakuchō Line). Conversely, because all Shinkiba-bound trains stop at every station from Nerima on the Seibu Yūrakuchō Line, they were announced as "Local" from Nerima and as "All-stations" from Kotake-mukaihara.
In the March 12, 2022 timetable revision, daytime Seibu Line through services were reduced from 6 to 4 round trips per hour, with the freed paths reassigned to the Shinkiba–Ikebukuro section, so Ikebukuro-terminating services were introduced during the day as well.

S-TRAIN
A reserved-seat service introduced on March 27, 2017, operating during weekday commuting hours. All trains run through to/from Toyosu via the Seibu Yūrakuchō and Ikebukuro lines. A reserved-seat ticket is required to board, and trains stop only at Iidabashi and Yūrakuchō en route (Ikebukuro is also passed; trains make a non-stop technical stop at Kotake-mukaihara for crew changes). At both stations, boarding is permitted only in the morning and alighting only in the evening, and travel solely within the Yurakucho Line is not possible. It is the first service type on the Yurakucho Line with passing stations since the Semi Express, which was abolished in 2010.
On weekends and holidays, S-TRAIN operates through on the Fukutoshin Line, Tōkyū Tōyoko Line, and Minatomirai Line (to/from Motomachi-Chūkagai) and does not enter the Yurakucho Line. In addition, because conductors are carried on S-TRAIN to check reserved-seat tickets, it is exempt from one-man operation.

Fukutoshin Line trains
Following the opening of the Fukutoshin Line, the Wakōshi–Kotake-mukaihara section of this line became shared with the Fukutoshin Line. Fukutoshin Line all-station, Commuter Express, and Express services also operate on this section. For details, see "Fukutoshin Line."

Main changes accompanying the opening of the Fukutoshin Line
With the opening of the Fukutoshin Line on June 14, 2008, a substantial timetable revision was also carried out on the Yurakucho Line, which has parallel and shared sections. The main changes were as follows.
The premium "Semi Express" service type was introduced (details below). The journey time between Wakōshi and Shinkiba was set at 49 minutes 35 seconds for Local trains and 45 minutes 20 seconds for Semi Express trains.
At Kotake-mukaihara Station, Yurakucho Line Shinkiba-bound and Fukutoshin Line Shibuya-bound trains, and Wakōshi-direction and Seibu Line through trains, were cross-connected. Before the opening of the Fukutoshin Line, Shinkiba-bound and Shin-Ikebukuro-bound trains, and Wakōshi-direction and Seibu Line through trains, had already been connected (although not on all services, both before and after the opening).
At Kotake-mukaihara Station, connections were no longer held when one train was delayed; scheduled connecting trains would not be held for each other if delayed. Before the opening of the Fukutoshin Line, connections had been held when one train was delayed.
More through services with the Tōbu Tōjō Line or Seibu lines changed service type at Wakōshi or Kotake-mukaihara.
The origins and termini of Seibu Line through services were changed and workings were restructured. Examples follow.
Local services saw more Kiyose arrivals/departures.
Replacing the daytime Shinkiba–Hanno (Rapid) and Shin-Ikebukuro–Kotesashi (Local) services, daytime patterns became Shinkiba–Kotesashi (Semi Express) and Shibuya–Hanno (Rapid).

Former service types
Limited express Romancecar "Bay Resort"
A portion of the Odakyū Electric Railway limited express Romancecar services, operated by the 60000 series "MSE" through to the Chiyoda Line, was diverted from Kita-Senju on the Chiyoda Line to run to Shinkiba on this line under the name "Bay Resort" for about 30 days a year.
Trains ran via the connecting line between Sakuradamon on the Yurakucho Line and Kasumigaseki on the Chiyoda Line (see below), reversing direction at Kasumigaseki. Within the Yurakucho Line, trains stopped only at Toyosu and Shinkiba.
Services were suspended from September 25, 2011, and were formally discontinued in the March 17, 2012 timetable revision.

Semi Express
Semi Express was not a designation from through-running destinations, but the first service type on the Yurakucho Line to include passing stations within the line itself. Introduced in the June 14, 2008 timetable revision, it operated on weekday daytime and at all times other than early mornings and late nights on weekends and holidays. Together with the parallel Fukutoshin Line Express and Commuter Express services, it was the fourth example of no-supplement premium services on a Tokyo subway, following the Tōzai Line Rapid, Toei Shinjuku Line Express, and Toei Asakusa Line Airport Limited Express.
Stopping stations were Wakōshi, Kotake-mukaihara, and all stations between Ikebukuro and Shinkiba.
The image color was yellow-green.
From its introduction, some services also ran through to/from the Tōbu Tōjō Line and Seibu lines. Frequencies were 3 trains per hour toward Shinkiba (2 from Wakōshi and 1 from Kotesashi) and 2 per hour each for Wakōshi/Tōjō Line and Seibu Line workings, operating on weekends and holidays until around 9 p.m., with 22 round trips on weekdays (44 on weekends and holidays). However, in the November 29, 2008 timetable revision, they were drastically reduced to 2 trains per hour in each direction during daytime only on both weekday and weekend timetables (10 round trips per day), all Semi Express services operated only between Wakōshi and Shinkiba, and Tōjō Line/Seibu Line through Semi Expresses and evening services were downgraded to Local. Furthermore, because the Semi Express reduced the number of stopping trains and travel opportunities at Kanamechō and Senkawa stations, the Toshima Ward Assembly, where the two stations are located, submitted an opinion paper requesting the complete abolition of the Semi Express. In response, Tokyo Metro announced its abolition in the March 6, 2010 timetable revision, and the Yurakucho Line Semi Express disappeared less than two years after its introduction.
Semi Expresses through-running onto the Tōjō Line changed to "Local" (普通) at Wakōshi Station and ran as local trains within the Tōjō Line (since stopping patterns matched Tōjō Line Semi Expresses, some 7000 series trains also ran displaying "Semi Express"; on Tōbu trains, full-color LED displays showed green for Yurakucho Line Semi Expresses and blue for Tōjō Line Semi Expresses). However, Tōjō Line through Semi Expresses were infrequent: on weekdays only a single one-way Shinkiba→Kawagoe-shi service ran, and on weekends and holidays only three early Kawagoe-shi→Shinkiba services and five round trips from the evening, with all but one weekend Shinrin-kōen-bound service running to/from Kawagoe-shi. Seibu Line through Semi Expresses, on the other hand, either ran as "Semi Express" within the Seibu network or changed to "All-stations" or "Rapid" at Kotake-mukaihara. They were also more frequent, centered on Kotesashi arrivals/departures, with some services running to/from Kiyose and Hanno.
Even after the abolition of the Yurakucho Line Semi Express, the Fukutoshin Line Express services (including F Liners) noted above continue as faster services stopping at Wakōshi, Kotake-mukaihara, and Ikebukuro.

Rolling stock
All current rolling stock is shared with the Fukutoshin Line. East of Kotake-mukaihara, in principle only 10-car Tokyo Metro, Seibu, and Tōbu trains enter, but on the Wakōshi–Kotake-mukaihara section and the parallel Kotake-mukaihara–Ikebukuro Fukutoshin Line tracks, 8-car Tokyo Metro, Tōkyū, Yokohama Minatomirai Railway, and Sagami Railway trains also enter.

Entered service on February 21, 2021. Replaced the 10-car 7000 series trains.

10000 series
Entered service on September 1, 2006. Principally formed as 10-car sets, but sets 01–05 can also operate as 8-car formations. However, like the 8-car 17000 series, 8-car operation is limited to specific workings and is not used on the Yurakucho Line.

7000 series trains running through on the Yurakucho Line were only 10-car sets with gold stripes, but by May 2010 (Heisei 22) all 10-car sets had been standardized for joint Fukutoshin Line/Yurakucho Line use, the gold-striped 7000 series disappeared, and Fukutoshin Line-colored trains were operated.
The 8-car trains rebuilt in preparation for the opening of the Fukutoshin Line were not used on Yurakucho Line workings, instead entering service as Fukutoshin Line locals on the shared Wakōshi–Kotake-mukaihara section.
Revenue operation ended in April 2022.

All trains had been transferred to the Tōzai Line by March 2009 (Heisei 21).

Before the opening of the Fukutoshin Line, too, all trains within the Yurakucho Line stopped at all stations, although the presence of service-type displays varied by rolling stock before the Fukutoshin Line opened. Usage
In fiscal 2021 (Reiwa 3), the congestion rate on the most crowded section (A line, between Higashi-Ikebukuro and Gokokuji) was 102%.
In fiscal 1987, when through operation with the Tōjō Line began, a congestion rate of 229% was recorded; increased capacity eased this to around 180% by fiscal 1993. Ridership declined from fiscal 1998 onward, and congestion fell below 170% in fiscal 2008, when the Fukutoshin Line opened.
In fiscal 2007, average daily passengers between Ikebukuro and Iidabashi exceeded 370,000, of which the Edogawabashi–Iidabashi section carried the most at 378,275. Ridership falls at Iidabashi, with 301,399 between Iidabashi and Ichigaya. It then exceeds 200,000 as far as Toyosu, falls again at Toyosu, and is 112,576 between Toyosu and Tatsumi. On the Wakōshi side, ridership falls beyond Ikebukuro; in particular, it drops at Kotake-mukaihara, where the Seibu Line branches off, with 229,420 between Hikawadai and Kotake-mukaihara. The decline continues thereafter, with 113,140 between Wakōshi and Chikatetsu Narimasu across the border with Saitama Prefecture. The lowest ridership is between Tatsumi and Shinkiba, at 92,483.

Local services stop at all stations and are therefore omitted.
Because interchange stations often require exiting the gates once or walking for extended periods within the station, transfers to other lines often take time, though transfers to the Namboku Line are comparatively smooth.
Although Shintomichō Station has an opposing-platform layout built by cut-and-cover, because the platforms lie beneath the Irifune Bridge there are no center pillars between tracks. This is a rare structure for an underground station in Japan; comparable examples include Hakusan on the Toei Mita Line and Minami-Senju and Aoi on the Tsukuba Express.
Because through travel from the Yūrakuchō Line via Ikebukuro–Kanamechō–Fukutoshin Line Ikebukuro does not permit turn-back transfers at Kanamechō, transfers between the Yurakucho Line toward Shinkiba and the Fukutoshin Line toward Shibuya require exiting the fare gates once at Ikebukuro.
Holding a commuter pass covering the Wakōshi–Ikebukuro section of this line permits travel on the same section of the Fukutoshin Line, and a pass covering Iidabashi–Ichigaya permits travel on the same section of the Namboku Line.
The reserved-seat service S-TRAIN permits boarding only toward Kotesashi on the Seibu Ikebukuro Line and alighting only from trains arriving from Tokorozawa; use solely within the Yurakucho Line is not permitted.
Wakōshi and Shinkiba are above-ground stations; all others are underground.

Connecting lines
This line has two connecting lines to other routes.

Lines 8 and 9 connecting siding
A connecting line that curves southwest from the west side of Sakuradamon Station, connecting on a single track to the west side of Kasumigaseki Station on the Chiyoda Line.
This connecting line is single track and 577.896 m long, with a tight curve of radius 167.595 m partway along it.

Connecting line to the Namboku Line running parallel southeast from Ichigaya Station
These two connecting lines primarily serve to return trains for inspection to the Ayase Works on the Chiyoda Line, but special trains also run very rarely. Since 2002, special trains linked to summer fireworks festivals and the New Year period have become a regular fixture. Because of the through-running relationships, these services use Chiyoda Line trains (16000 series, formerly 06 and 6000 series) when through from the Chiyoda Line, and Namboku Line trains (9000 series) when through from the Namboku Line. The latter connecting line was also used to return 8000 series trains for the Hanzōmon Line to be refurbished at Shinkiba CR. This empty-stock movement runs from Sagamihara Depot via the Tōkyū Den-en-toshi, Ōimachi, and Meguro lines and the Namboku Line, entering the Yurakucho Line via the connecting line to Shinkiba.

kono決定wo受ke、営団地下鉄ha1962年（Showa37年）10月16日、同時ni都市計画wo決定shita第7号線（南北線）totomoni、第8号線谷原町 - 江東橋間（都市計画上no中村橋kara西niyaya延伸shita20.88 km）toshite地方鉄道敷設免許wo申請shita。後ni両路線tomo東京都（東京都交通局）mo路線免許wo申請shitakotokara、競願状態tonaru。

konouchi、小竹向原駅 - 新木場駅間ga有楽町線、練馬駅 - 小竹向原駅間ga西武有楽町線、石神井公園駅 - 練馬駅間ga西武Ikebukuro Station線no線増分（複々線化）toshitesorezoreopenedshiteiru。terminus側ha京葉間no湾岸沿ini海浜nyutaun付近made計画sareteitaga、hobo同jirutode計画sareteita京葉線ga当時ha貨物専用線toshite計画ga進行shiteori、後ni旅客線heto用途ga変更saretakotowo受kete有楽町線ha新木場madeno計画路線ni短縮shita。

Heiwadai Station - Ikebukuro Station間deha東京都no街路事業（都市計画道路）to地下鉄no建設wo同時ni施工suru予定deata。shikashi、現道ganaku新tani道路wo整備suruHikawadai Station - 千川間deha、周辺住民kara排気gasuya騒音wo懸念shite計画道路heno反対ga根強ku、道路計画ni地下鉄建設mo巻ki込marete用地交渉ha難航shita。tadashi、地下鉄建設niha賛成no住民ga多kata。最終的nihaoirushokuno影響niyote東京都no財政ga急激ni悪化shi、道路整備ha困難tonatakotokara、営団地下鉄ha1975年（Showa50年）9月ni地下鉄wo先行shite建設shi、東京都no計画道路ha地下鉄建設後ni改mete整備surukotoni変更shita。

建設目的no一tsuniha、車体規格ga小saku編成長mo短ikotokara輸送力増強ni限界noaru丸no内線no混雑緩和gaata。Ikebukuro Stationno乗ri換ega便利deatatame、日比谷線ni対suru千代田線同様、混雑no緩和ni大kiku寄与shita。

mata、1974年（Showa49年）no銀座一丁目 - Ikebukuro Station間noopenedniatari、丸no内線中野坂上駅、日比谷線恵比寿駅ni次ide、Ikebukuro Stationni4基、銀座一丁目駅ni2基no自動改札機ga設置sareta。koreha、当該区間deha他線tono改札内連絡ganakatatame、集改札自動化no実証実験線区toshite好適deatatamedearu。両端駅dearuIkebukuro Station、銀座一丁目駅以外niha自動改札機ha設置sarenakataga、有楽町線no全駅de磁気化券ga発売sareteori、普通乗車券niyoru出場nimo対応shiteita。shikashi、当時ha他no路線deno乗車券no磁気化ga進ndeorazu、効率的na運用gadekinakatakotokara、営団成増（現, 地下鉄成増）延伸時ni一旦撤去sare、当時no試miha失敗ni終wateiru。sono他、大手町駅de採用sareta案内sainshisutemuwo全面的ni採用shita。

軌道構造
当路線dehaJNR（当時, Japanese National Railways (JNR)）wo除ki、地下鉄, 私鉄de初mete60 kgreruwo採用shita（本線部）。60 kgreruwo採用surukotode、reruno強度ga1.5倍、耐用年数ha4 - 6年長kunaru。軌道構造ha地下区間deha従来kara直結軌道wo採用shitekitaga、振動, 騒音ga大kiikotokara、本路線deha新tani"防振makuragi構造"wo採用shita（民有地近辺）。初期hareruto枕木no間nigomupadowo、枕木ha防振gomude覆umonodeataga、新富町opened以降、枕木部hareru支持部下ni防振gomu、防振pado、防振kushonkara構成sareru防振装置wo敷ki、reru間下wo中空toshita新shii構造wo採用shita。barasuto軌道区間nioitemo、軌道下ni防振matomataha防振shitowo敷ki、izuremo振動, 騒音低減ni大kina効果wo発揮shita。

都市交通審議会答申第15号deToyosu Station - 亀有間 (14.7 km) ga追加saretakotowo受ke、営団地下鉄ha1982年（Showa57年）1月29日nikono区間no鉄道事業免許wo申請shiteiru。

1985年（Showa60年）7月11日no運輸政策審議会答申第7号nioite、第8号線ha、Toyosu Stationkara北he分岐suru路線ga住吉 - 四tsu木間de第11号線（半蔵門線）to線路wo共用shi常磐線亀有駅（saraniJR武蔵野線方面）he至ru路線ni変更sareteori、Toyosu Stationto半蔵門線住吉駅ha線路ga分岐dekiruyou2面4線no構造de建設sareteiru。

沿線自治体tonaru江東区, 墨田区, 葛飾区, 松戸市no3区1市（及bi東京都, 千葉県no1都1県）ha1986年（Showa61年）ni"地下鉄8, 11号線促進連絡協議会"wo組織shi、2007年, 2008年（Heisei19年, Heisei20年）ni実施shita調査no結果、同協議会ga推進suru8号線, 11号線no延伸計画nouchi、Toyosu Station - 住吉駅間（約5.2 km）karano段階的na整備wo要望suru方針wo示shi、早期事業化wo目指shita活動ga行wareteiru。uchi、江東区（当該先行区間唯一no沿線自治体）ha地下鉄8号線no建設oyobi関連付帯設備ni要suru経費ni充terutametoshite、"（仮称）江東区地下鉄8号線建設基金"wo設置shi、Heisei22年度（2010年度）予算ni5億円wo計上shita。mata、Toyosu Station市場wo受ke入reru条件nimonateirutoshite東京都nadoni早期no延伸実現wo強ku求meteiru。

tadashi、東京metoroha2009年（Heisei21年）度3月期no有価証券報告書nioite申請時kara事業環境no変化wo理由ni"整備主体tonarukotoha極mete困難"to事業化ni消極的na態度wo表明shiteita。

江東区ha2011年7月ni第三sekutawo設立shite整備wo担i、運営wo行u上下分離方式de整備shi、Toyosu Station - 東陽町間（枝川付近）、東陽町 - 住吉間（千田付近）ni新駅wo建設suru計画案womatometa。2012年8月現在、江東区, 東京都, 東京metoronadoto検討委員会wo作ri協議中de、2015年度madeno着工wo目指shiteita。

2021年ni国土交通省ga交通政策審議会鉄道部会内ni設keta"東京圏niokeru今後no地下鉄netowakunoari方等ni関suru小委員会"nioite東京metorono完全民営化（株式売却）to並行shite都心部, 品川地下鉄構想to共ni有楽町線no延伸計画ni触rerareteori、2021年7月8日行wareta第5回小委員会to、同年7月15日ni示sareta"東京圏niokeru今後no地下鉄netowakunoari方等nitsuite"答申nioite、同区間nitsuite東京metoroga主体tonate整備wo進merunoga適切datosuru素案wo示sutotomoni、国ya東京都ga建設費wo補助suru方向性wo示shita。

事業費ha2019年時点no試算de1560億円daga、建築資材ya人件費no高騰de膨ramu見込mitonari、事業費no4分no3wo国ya都ga支援shi、東京metorono借入金niha財政投融資wo充teru方針dearu。2022年1月8日niha、延伸ni向keta作業ga同年4月kara本格的ni始maru見通shininata。 2022年度ha地質調査ya環境影響評価nadowo行i、具体的na金額ha2021年度末ni決maruga、国to都de計十数億円no見通shitoshiteiru。国ha2022年度no予算案ni環境影響nadono調査wo補助suru費用wo計上shi、都mo新年度予算案ni同様no費用wo盛ri込mu方針dearu。東京metoroha2022年（Reiwa4年）1月28日niToyosu Station - 住吉間約4.8 kmno鉄道事業許可wo国土交通大臣ni申請shi、同年3月28日ni第一種鉄道事業no許可wo受keta。opened時期ha2030年代半bade、事業費ha2689億8200万円wo予定shiteiru。補助金ga1738億3200万円、財政投融資資金kara951億5000万円wo見込ndeiru。

新tana駅toshite、（仮称）枝川駅（Toyosu Stationstarting point1.250 km）、（仮称）東陽町駅（Toyosu Stationstarting point3.070 km）、（仮称）千石駅（Toyosu Stationstarting point4.180 km）no3駅wo設置suru。mata、東陽町ha同名no駅gaaru東西線no地下ni新駅ga作rare、乗換駅tonaru。運転間隔ha1時間atari日中de約8本、朝nopiku時de約12本wo予定shiteiru。本線heno乗ri入re本数ha今後検討surutoshi、半蔵門線乗ri入reha現時点deha検討sareteinai。

本路線ni係ru損益haopened14年目de単年度損益ga黒字転換、opened29年目ni累積損益ga黒字転換shi、累積損益収支haopened29年目ni黒字転換、累積資金収支haopened40年目ni黒字転換wo想定shiteiru。

住吉駅以遠nitsuiteha、八潮駅（tsukubaekusupuresu）, 越谷reikutaun駅（武蔵野線）wo経由suru形deno延伸mo検討sareteiru。現在notokoro構想段階deari、運輸政策審議会答申第18号deha"2015年madeni整備着手surukotoga適当dearu路線"to位置付keraretaga、決定hanasareteinai。

Operations
Wakōshi Stationkara東武東上線wo経由shite川越市駅（朝夕ha森林公園駅）made、小竹向原駅karaha西武有楽町線経由Ikebukuro Station線直通de小手指駅（朝, 夕no一部列車ha飯能駅）madesorezore相互乗ri入rewo行teiru。

有楽町線nomino運行tonaru列車ya東武東上線直通列車ha全区間各駅停車de運行sareteiruga、西武Ikebukuro Station線直通列車ha西武線内wo準急, 快速, 快速急行toshite運行suru列車gaari、kono場合ha小竹向原駅de種別変更wo行u。mata後述suruyouni2017年3月25日kara有料指定列車"S-TRAIN"ga運転開始sareta。有楽町線heha平日daiyanomi乗ri入re、小手指駅 - Toyosu Station間de朝ni所沢発Toyosu Station行ki2本, 夕方以降niToyosu Station発小手指行kiwo5本運転shiteiru。有楽町線内no途中停車駅haIidabashi Station, 有楽町駅no2駅de、Toyosu Station行ha降車専用、小手指行ha乗車専用tonari、西武線内nomiya有楽町線内nomino利用ha不可能dearu。

Wakōshi Station - 小竹向原駅間ha副都心線to線路, 駅施設wo共有shi、新木場駅発着no列車to渋谷方面（東急東横線, minatomirai線, 東急新横浜線, 相鉄線直通）no列車gatomoni運行sareteiru。

副都心線tono共用区間dearuWakōshi Station - 小竹向原間deha10両編成to8両編成no列車de運行sareteiruga、小竹向原 - 新木場間hasubete10両編成no列車de運行sareteiru。

平日朝norashu時noIkebukuro Station方面deha数多kuno列車ga運行sare、小竹向原駅de新木場方面to渋谷方面ni振ri分kerareteiru。

有楽町線・副都心線が乗り入れる。当駅を含む小竹向原駅 - 池袋駅間は、有楽町線が上層を、副都心線が下層を走る形で並走する。このため、当駅においても有楽町線ホームの直下に副都心線のホームがある。駅番号は有楽町線がY 07、副都心線がF 07である。

章节.歴史:
1983年（昭和58年）6月24日：帝都高速度交通営団（営団地下鉄）有楽町線営団成増駅（現・地下鉄成増駅） - 池袋駅間の開通により開業。
 2003年（平成15年）2月：業務委託駅となる。
 2004年（平成16年）4月1日：帝都高速度交通営団（営団地下鉄）民営化に伴い、当駅は東京地下鉄（東京メトロ）に継承される。
 2007年（平成19年）3月18日：ICカード「PASMO」の利用が可能となる。
 2008年（平成20年）6月14日：副都心線の駅が開業（線路は1994年に通過線として開通済み）。
 2014年（平成26年）2月8日：有楽町線ホームのホームドアと発車メロディの使用を開始。
 2016年（平成28年）2月14日：当駅 - 小竹向原駅間の有楽町線和光市方面連絡線が完成し、始発から運用が開始される。
章节.駅構造:
上下2層構造で、各層に島式ホーム1面2線を有する地下駅。要町通りの直下にある。

現在の副都心線ホームは有楽町線建設時に既に構築済みであったが、1994年に小竹向原駅 - 池袋駅間が有楽町線新線として開業した時点では未供用（全列車通過）であり、2008年の副都心線開業時に内装整備の上、供用が開始された。副都心線開業までは、有楽町線ホームから副都心線ホームへの階段用スペースは蓋で覆われ、改札口 - ホーム間のエレベーターも有楽町線ホーム階止まりとして運用されていた。また、副都心線開業および有楽町線和光市駅 - 池袋駅間の準急運転開始に伴い有楽町線ホームの放送機器が更新され、編成両数を案内するようになった。ただし、有楽町線内での準急運転は2010年3月で廃止している。

中文.首段:
千川站（せんかわえき）是位于日本东京都丰岛区要町三丁目，属于东京地下铁的铁路车站。

此站有有乐町线、副都心线停靠。包括此站的小竹向原站－池袋站路段，有乐町线在上层而副都心线在下层行走。因此此站的有乐町线月台的正下方就是副都心线月台。有乐町线的车站编号是Y 07、副都心线是F 07。

章节.历史:
1983年（昭和58年）6月24日：营团地下铁有乐町线千川站开业。
 2003年（平成15年）2月：成为业务委托站。
 2004年（平成16年）4月1日：营团地下铁民营化，本站由东京地下铁接手经营。
 2008年（平成20年）6月14日：副都心线站区启用。
 2014年（平成26年）2月8日：有乐町线设置可动式月台门。有乐町线全线车站皆设置月台门。
 2016年（平成28年）2月14日：本站－小竹向原站间的有乐町线和光市方向联络线完成并启用。
章节.车站构造:
本站位于要町通的地下，月台采双层岛式月台的设计：上层为有乐町线月台，下层为副都心线，与小竹向原－池袋段其他车站相同。其中副都心线月台实际上与有乐町线月台一同落成，但直到副都心线通车时才开放使用。因此，有乐町线月台往副都心线月台的楼梯空间皆被遮蔽。剪票口至月台间的电梯虽能通至副都心线月台，但当时上仅开放至有乐町线本线（当时）月台。另外，随著副都心线通车与有乐町线和光市站 - 池袋站间的准急开始运行。有乐町线月台的广播机器也随之更新，广播内容加入列车编组长度。但有乐町线内的准急已在2010年3月废止。

2014年2月8日，本站启用月台门，从此有乐町站所有车站皆导入月台门。副都心线月台在启用时就已设置月台门。
章节.月台配置:
（来源：东京地下铁:构内图）

 平日早晨尖峰时刻，本站有2班始发列车，但没有本站终停的班次。该列车是利用小竹向原站 - 本站间的中线折返后，再进入本站载客。误点时，可能会有本站终停的班次。
 本站虽是有乐町线与副都心线的车站，但副都心线并没有显示转乘资讯，仅在广播后加上「本站转乘有乐町线」。
 有乐町线月台小竹向原侧的A线（新木场方向）及B线（和光市）上设有转辙器，转辙器外侧由往小竹向原站1号线、4号线的列车使用。转辙器内侧主要由往小竹向原站2号线、3号线的列车使用。过去该地点有保线机器使用的侧线，现在已移往连络线的小竹向原侧起点附近。
 副都心线月台小竹向原侧有保线机器使用的侧线。
章节.发车音乐: 副都心线月台（3、4号线）自开业起、有乐町线月台（1、2号线）自2014年2月8日起，使用株式会社SWITCH的发车音乐。

日文.首段:
和光市駅（わこうしえき）は、埼玉県和光市本町にある、東武鉄道・東京地下鉄（東京メトロ）の駅である。





 東武鉄道 和光市駅
 和光市駅/Y01/F01 | 路線・駅の情報 | 東京メトロ

章节.概要:
東武鉄道の東上本線と、東京メトロの有楽町線・副都心線が乗り入れる。当駅 - 小竹向原駅の区間は、東京メトロ有楽町線と副都心線が線路を共有している。駅番号は、東武東上本線がTJ 11、東京メトロ有楽町線がY 01、副都心線がF 01である。

東武鉄道と東京メトロの共同使用駅で東武鉄道の管轄駅である。東京メトロの駅としては最北端かつ最西端に位置する駅であり、東京の地下鉄全体でも最西端に位置し、唯一埼玉県内に所在する駅である

東武川越駅管区傘下の駅長配置駅（東武川越駅副管区長兼務）。
章节.駅開業から終戦まで:
1914年（大正3年）5月1日に東上鉄道（現・東武東上本線）池袋駅 - 田面沢駅の開業から大幅に遅れて、1934年（昭和9年）2月1日に埼玉県新座郡新倉村ににいくら駅として開業したのが始まりである。開業直後の同年7月12日に新倉駅へ変更した。

開業当時の当駅近隣の集落は白子宿など川越街道沿いに存在しており、駅は畑の中に開設された。そのため、開業当初の一日平均の乗客は約94人で、1938年（昭和13年）には約160人であった。

大日本帝国陸軍が白子村と新倉村の全面積の約20%に相当する土地について1937年（昭和12年）から買収を進め、1941年（昭和16年）11月2日に陸軍予科士官学校が移転し、1940年（昭和15年）に大倉財閥系で機関銃を製造していた「中央工業新倉工場」や「芝浦工作機械」「日興航空工業」など多くの軍需工場も進出し、駅の南側を中心として人口も増加した。1945年（昭和20年）には、一日平均の乗客は開業時の20倍以上に増加した。
章节.戦後の状況:
第二次世界大戦で敗戦したことにより、1945年（昭和20年）8月に陸軍予科士官学校は解散され、軍需産業は壊滅状態となった。しかし陸軍予科士官学校跡地や中央工業新倉工場跡地などが米軍に接収され、キャンプ・ドレイクとして米軍第一騎兵師団約4,000人が進駐し、1960年（昭和35年）3月には陸上自衛隊朝霞駐屯地が開設されたことから、戦後も軍需都市的な側面が残った。

一方、本田技研工業が1952年（昭和27年）3月に「日興精機工業」の工場を買収して白子工場を開設し、1953年（昭和28年）7月に中央工業新倉工場跡地の一部を買収して大和工場を開設するなど民需工場の進出も相次ぎ、当駅周辺は新たな発展を遂げた。

その後、米軍基地返還跡地に日本住宅公団が1965年（昭和40年）4月「西大和団地」を開設したのを皮切りに、「南大和団地」や「諏訪原団地」が開設された。「米軍新倉倉庫」となっていた中央工業新倉工場跡地の一部が1971年（昭和46年）6月23日に返還され、翌1972年（昭和47年）にその土地を取得した伊藤忠商事が「シーアイハイツ和光」として再開発を行うなど、返還された米軍基地の跡地には多数の団地開発が進められた。

また、1941年（昭和16年）7月20日に開院した白子陸軍病院が1945年（昭和20年）12月1日に厚生省に移管され、一般市民向けの医療施設「国立埼玉病院」として存続し、米軍基地返還跡地の一部に1967年（昭和42年）3月に理化学研究所（理研）が大和研究所を開設するなど、公共系の施設も当駅周辺に立地した。

さらに、松ノ木島地区や丸山台地区などで土地区画整理事業が進められ、新興住宅地としても発展した。

この間、1951年（昭和26年）10月に新倉村の合併による大和町の発足を受けて「大和町駅」（やまとまちえき）に改称された。
章节.都営地下鉄・東急電鉄との相互乗り入れ計画:
こうした利用者の増加に対応して輸送力増強を行うため、1964年（昭和39年）1月には当駅と東京都板橋区志村の間に東武東上支線（1969年に板橋区の住居表示実施により高島平の町名が発足してからは仮称・東武高島平線）を建設する計画が立てられた。この計画には東武東上本線と都営地下鉄6号線（現・三田線）、および東京急行電鉄（現・東急）田園都市線（現・大井町線）・池上線において相互直通運転を行う内容が盛り込まれていた。

しかし、東京都交通局が1968年（昭和43年）12月27日に巣鴨 - 志村（現・高島平）間を開通させた後、東武鉄道は6号線計画について、都心へ向けて大きく迂回するルートであること、および池袋駅を経由しないために、東武百貨店をはじめとした池袋地区の開発に資さず、東上本線にとっての線増効果が見込めないことを理由として、都交通局に相互乗り入れ計画撤回を申し入れた。都交通局側は難色を示したが、1972年（昭和47年）3月1日に都市交通審議会が運輸大臣に提出した都市交通審議会答申第15号において、東京6号線建設予定計画が「高島平 - 戸田市西部 - 浦和市西部…大宮市西部」に変更されたことにより、当駅 - 高島平間4.8kmの東武高島平線計画は正式に撤回された。高島平駅が2面4線のホームとなっているのは、この計画の名残りである。東武鉄道が保有していた同線免許のうち、高島平駅 - 三園町駅間1.5kmについては1973年（昭和48年）4月に都交通局へ譲渡され、都営地下鉄6号線高島平 - 西高島平間として1976年（昭和51年）5月に開通した。

この間、1970年（昭和45年）12月に市制施行・新市名制定を受けて、「和光市駅」に改称された。
章节.営団地下鉄との相互乗り入れ:
一方、1969年（昭和44年）1月に帝都高速度交通営団が営団地下鉄8号線（現・有楽町線）の車庫を「米軍新倉倉庫」跡地の一部に設置し、そのための引込線を東武東上本線に沿って建設する構想で用地の取得を申し入れた。同線の建設計画は、1968年（昭和43年）10月に営団が免許を取得した時点では「明石町（現・新富町駅）- 永田町駅 - 飯田橋駅 - 池袋駅 - 成増駅」とされており、当駅への乗り入れは含まれていなかった。

1970年（昭和45年）4月10日に営団が当時の大和町当局に示した当初の構想では、東上本線に沿う形で高架線を建設し、駅を開設せず旅客扱いを行わないものであった。そのため町当局が反発し、旅客扱いや車庫地下化など7項目の要求を行い、受け入れられない場合には車庫の建設を認めないと表明した。

その後1975年（昭和50年）10月に営団が当駅から渋谷駅までの路線（第13号線）の建設許可を申請し、1976年（昭和51年）8月11日に運輸大臣から営団に事業免許が交付され、1978年（昭和53年）7月11日には第8号線（現・有楽町線）の建設許可も交付された。これを受けて和光市も地下鉄乗り入れに伴う駅周辺の整備事業に乗り出し、渋滞解消のための立体交差や土地区画整理などの調整を始めた。立体交差化について、当初は高さ4.5mの地下道を建設することが構想されたものの、商店街への影響を避けるため、鉄道側を1.85m嵩上げすることで地下道の高さを維持したままで深さを抑制する計画へ変更され、1985年（昭和60年）8月5日に地下市道が開通した。

さらに新線建設や乗り入れに向けた駅の改築工事などを進め、1987年（昭和62年）8月25日に有楽町線が営団成増駅（現・地下鉄成増駅）から当駅まで延伸開業し、相互直通運転が始められた。

その後、2008年（平成20年）6月14日に副都心線が全線開通して、当駅から東武東上本線との相互直通運転が始まり、2013年（平成25年）3月16日に渋谷駅地下ホームが完成したことにより、副都心線を経由して東急東横線との間の相互直通運転も始まった。

章节.駅構造:
南口のみで営業していたが、営団地下鉄の乗り入れに合わせた改良工事で路盤全体を嵩上げして半高架化し、北口の開設や地下市道の建設と合わせた立体交差による踏切の廃止などが行われた。

和光市のウェブサイト「まちの景観変遷」に掲載された画像が示す通り、有楽町線開業以前は島式ホーム1面2線で、現上りホームの位置にホームがあり、駅舎は現在の南口側、現下りホームの場所にあった。改築に伴い、駅本屋および改札口は池袋寄りに移動した。

島式ホーム2面4線を有する高架駅。半高架式。ホーム直下に改札口があり、改札からは階段（スロープあり）を上って駅舎外に出る構造となっている。池袋方階段に上りエスカレーターが設置されている。駅売店は改札外の自動券売機横にある。

有楽町線の延伸開業に併せて大改良を行った際に、いち早く身体障害者対応のエレベーターを設置した。しかし、設置位置の関係から出口は改札外となっていたことから、係員の付き添いがないと利用することができなかったが、改札内にエレベーターの設置工事を施工し、2005年10月から使用を開始した。

当駅 - 志木駅間は、東上本線内で唯一の複々線区間である。朝霞駅側に有楽町線・副都心線列車の引き上げ線が2線あり、線路はその先の和光検車区に続いている。

有楽町線・副都心線には当駅発着列車が設定されているのに対して、東上本線の当駅発着列車は配線の関係上設定されていない。地下鉄線内の当駅発着は平日日中および土日祝日でも1時間に10本あり（うち4本が東上本線直通）、ラッシュ時やダイヤが乱れた場合を中心にB線で当駅から列車が数珠繋ぎになる場合がある。

章节.備考:
上下ともに東上本線と有楽町線・副都心線は同一ホームで乗り換えが可能である。
 8両編成は、ホームの地下鉄成増寄り2両分には停車しない。

章节.構内放送:
3番線（有楽町線・副都心線のりば）では有楽町線開通当初から、それ以外では朝ラッシュ時のみ4番線で発車ベルが使用されていた。

2007年4月5日に東上線ホーム（1・2・4番線）に、東武オリジナルの発車メロディが導入された。3番線には2012年7月7日のホームドア稼働開始と同時にスイッチ制作の発車メロディ「きらめくホーム」（福嶋尚哉作曲）が導入されたが、同年12月17日に再びベルに戻された。その後、2023年10月24日に東武オリジナルの発車メロディに変更され、再びすべてのホームで発車メロディが流れるようになった。
章节.利用状況:
1日平均の乗降人員は以下の通りである。数値は、東武鉄道⇔東京メトロとの直通連絡人員を含んでおり、実際の駅自体の利用者数はこれよりも少ない。
 東武鉄道 - 2021年度の1日平均乗降人員は138,207人である。
 東武鉄道の駅の中では池袋駅、北千住駅に次いで第3位。
 東京メトロ - 2022年度の1日平均乗降人員は156,740人である。
章节.南口:
当駅の中心的な出口である南口は、区画整理が完了したことに伴い、南口を中心に多くの商業ビル、銀行などが立地するようになった。

前述のように駅の南側にはかつて軍の施設や軍需工場があったことからまとまった土地があり、その跡地に理化学研究所や本田技術研究所などの国や民間の施設が立地した。そのため南口からは多くの研究所方面行きのバスが発着している。

章节.北口: 北口駅前周辺は、道路が狭く住宅が密集しているなど多くの問題を抱えていることから、和光市では2008年度から北口土地区画整理事業を進めている。今後、新たに駅前交通広場を設け商業系・住居系土地利用の増進、道路や公園などの整備を行っていく予定である。
章节.バス路線: 北口と南口に和光市駅停留所があり、以下の路線バスが発着する。一般路線バスは東武バスウエストと西武バス、空港連絡バスは西武バス・東京空港交通・京成バス・東武バスウエストにより運行されている。南口は研究所方面行きのバスが多く発着する。国際興業バスも池袋駅西口発深夜急行バスが南口に乗り入れている。

章节.付記:
東上本線に乗り入れない西武鉄道の車両（6000系・40000系）及び2023年3月18日ダイヤ改正以降に東急新横浜線・相鉄新横浜線との相互直通運転開始に合わせて乗り入れた相鉄20000系も東京メトロ線の当駅までは入線可能であるため、当駅で折り返す運用が設定されている。
 2016年3月26日のダイヤ改正までは、有楽町線・副都心線 - 東上本線の直通列車については有楽町線内では「各停」、副都心線内では「各停」「急行」「通勤急行」のいずれかになるのに対し、東上本線内では「普通」となっていたため、全列車が当駅で種別変更されていた。
 東武東上本線の都内区間（成増 - 池袋間）で何らかの運行トラブルが発生した場合、地下鉄直通列車のみ（当駅 - 川越市駅間）を先に運転再開することがある。ただし、2010年3月改正から2011年3月5日改正の間までは、日中時間帯に川越市まで乗り入れる地下鉄線直通列車の運転間隔が大きく開く場合があった。
 東京メトロでは有楽町線全駅へホームドアの設置を進めており、当駅への設置について東武鉄道と調整中としていた。その後、2番線ホームには2012年4月14日に、3番線ホームには同年4月21日にそれぞれ設置され、同年7月7日に稼働を開始した。その後、4番線ホームには2016年2月14日に、1番線ホームにも同年2月21日に設置され、同年3月26日に稼働を開始した。
 東武東上本線内の駅（朝霞 - 森林公園間）では、副都心線経由で渋谷より先の東急東横線の連絡乗車券は発売していないが、東京メトロ副都心線各駅（東急電鉄管轄の渋谷駅を除く）では東急東横線横浜駅まで発売しているため、当駅は東武鉄道管轄であるものの、東京メトロの駅としても扱われているため、東武東上線内で唯一東急東横線各駅までの乗車券を発売している。なお、横浜から先の横浜高速鉄道みなとみらい線各駅までは東武鉄道も東京メトロも連絡乗車券は発売していない。
 2016年に理化学研究所和光本所が新元素「ニホニウム」を発見・命名したことに記念して、当駅から理化学研究所和光本所までの間にニホニウム通りが整備された。
